19:1: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Kaf from Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad. Some of them said: The interpretation of that is that it is a letter from His name, which is great, by which He indicated it, and by mentioning it there was no need to mention the rest of the name. Who said that? Abu Hasin Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Yunus told me, he said: Abthar told us, he said: Hasin told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad, he said: Great, meaning by great is the kaf of Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad. Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ismail bin Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, the same. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: Hisin told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: He used to say Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad. He said: Kaf means great. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ismail bin Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad, he said: Kaf means great. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar. Others said: Rather, the Kaf in that is a letter from the letters of his name, which is Kaf. Who said that? Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me: Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed, regarding his statement, Kaf, Ha, Ain, Sad, he said: Kaf: Kaf. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said: Abu Rawq told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, regarding his statement, Kaf, Ha, Ain, Sad, he said: Kaf: Kaf. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Al-Kalbi, similarly. Others said: Rather, it is a letter from the letters of his name, which is Generous. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad he said: Kaf from Karim. Those who interpreted this interpretation said that the letter ha in Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad is a letter from the letters of His name, which is Haad. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: Abu Hasin told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: He used to say about the ha’ in Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad “Haad.” Abu Haseen told us, he said: Abthar told us, he said: Haseen told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Hanad told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Saeed, the same. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ismail bin Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, something similar. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Yahya bin Talha told me: Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: Ha: This is it. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said: Abu Rawq told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, regarding his statement, Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad, he said: Ha: Haad. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us: Anbasa told us, on the authority of Al-Kalbi, the same. They differed in the interpretation of the letter ya in this. Some of them said: It is a letter from the letters of his name, which is Yamin. Who said that? Abu Haseen told me, he said: Abthar told us, he said: Haseen told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: O you who Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad is a Ya of the right. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: Hisin told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Hanad told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ismail bin Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, similarly. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ismail bin Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: Ya: oath. Others said: Rather, it is a letter of the letters of His name, which is Al-Hakim. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad he said: O: Who is the Wise. Others said: Rather, it is a letter from the saying of the speaker: O He who protects. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Ibrahim bin Al-Durais told us: I heard Al-Rabi’ bin Anas regarding his statement, Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad, saying: O He who grants protection but is not granted protection. The interpreters of this also differed regarding the meaning of the eye. Some of them said: It is a letter of the letters of His name, which is All-Knowing. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed: Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad he said: An eye from the world. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Al-Kalbi, the same. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: Hisin told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Amr told us: Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-Ala bin Al-Musayyab bin Rafi’, on the authority of his father, regarding his statement, Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad, he said: Ain: from the world. Others said: Rather, it is a letter from the letters of His name, which is Aziz. Who said that? Abu Haseen told me, he said: Abthar told us, he said: Haseen told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad ‘Ain means Mighty. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ismail bin Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, similarly. Hanad told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ismail bin Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, similarly. Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me: Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement, Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad, he said: The eye of Mighty. Others said: Rather, it is a letter from the letters of His name, which is Adl. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said: Abu Rawq told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, regarding His statement, Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad, he said: “Ain: justice.” Those who interpreted this interpretation said: The letter sad in His saying Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad is a letter from the letters of His name, which is Sadiq. The novel mentioned that: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: Husayn told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: He used to say in Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad Sad: Truthful. Abu Haseen told me, he said: Abthar told us, he said: Haseen told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Hanad told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ismail bin Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, similarly. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ismail bin Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, the same. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said: Abu Rawq told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, he said: Sad: truthful. Yahya bin Talha told me: Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed, who said: Truthful, meaning the letter sad in Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed: Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad means: Sad is truthful. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us: Anbasa told us, on the authority of Al-Kalbi: He is truthful. Others said: Rather, this entire word is one of the names of God Almighty. Who said that? Muhammad bin Khalid bin Khidash told me: Salim bin Qutaybah told me, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, on the authority of Aatika, on the authority of Fatima, the daughter of Ali, who said: Ali used to say: O Kaha Ya Ain Sad, forgive me. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Concerning his statement: Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad, he said: It is an oath by which God swears, and it is one of the names of God. Others said: Each letter of this is a name of God Almighty. Who said that? Matar bin Muhammad Al-Dhabi told me: Abd Al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Aziz bin Muslim Al-Qasmali, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, who said: Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad is not a letter in it except that it is a noun. Others said: This word is one of the names of the Qur’an. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad, he said: It is one of the names of the Qur’an. Abu Ja`far said: Our statement on this is similar to our statement on the openings of the chapters of the Qur’an that begin with the letters of the alphabet. We have mentioned this before, so there is no need to repeat it here.
19:2: Arabists differed about the nominative of the male and the accusative of the slave. Some grammarians of Basra said about the meaning of that it is as if he said: What you have missed is the mention of your Lord's mercy on His slave, and the slave is made accusative by mercy as you say: He mentioned Zaid's beating of Amr. Some grammarians of Kufa said: The male is raised by Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad, and if you wish you can imply this is the mention of your Lord's mercy. He said: The meaning is that your Lord mentioned His slave with His mercy, advancing and delaying. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement in my opinion is to say: The male is raised by an omitted pronoun, which is this, as He did in other surahs, such as the statement of God, A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger, and His statement, A surah We have sent down, and the like. The servant is in the accusative case because of mercy, and Zachariah is in the accusative case because it is a statement about the servant, so the interpretation of the statement is: This is a mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zachariah.
19:3: And his saying, When he called upon his Lord with a secret call, means when he called upon his Lord and asked Him with a secret call, meaning: while he was secretly calling upon Him and asking Him for what he asked for, out of his hatred for showing off. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, When he called upon his Lord a secret call, meaning secretly, and God knows the pure heart and hears the secret voice. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement, When he called upon his Lord with a secret call, he said: He did not mean hypocrisy.
19:4: Musa bin Harun narrated to us, he said: Amr bin Hammad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: Zachariah desired a child, so he stood up and prayed, then he called upon his Lord secretly, saying: My Lord, indeed my bones have become feeble to And make him, my Lord, pleasing. And His saying: “He said: My Lord, indeed my bones have become feeble,” God Almighty says, so his secret call with which he called upon his Lord was that he said: My Lord, indeed my bones have become feeble, meaning by his saying weak weakness and frailty from old age. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, He said, ‘My Lord, indeed my bones have become feeble.’ That is, my bones have become weak. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And my bones have become weak, he said: The bones have become thin. Abd al-Razzaq said: Al-Thawri said: It has reached me that Zakariya was seventy years old. The Arabists differed about the reason for the accusative case of ash-shayb. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is accusative as a source of meaning of the speech, as if when he said ash-shayb, he said ash-shayb, and then said ash-shayban as a source. He said: It is not in the meaning of I burst fat and filled with water, because that is not a source. Another said: It is accusative of ash-shayb as an explanation, because it is said: The gray hair of my head burst and My head burst with gray hair, just as it is said: I burst fat and My fat burst. And his saying, And I have never been wretched in my supplication to You, O Lord, means: And I have never been wretched, O Lord, in my supplication to You, because You have never disappointed my supplication before when I called upon You in my need of You, but rather You answered and fulfilled my need before You. As Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement, And I have never been, through my supplication to You, my Lord, unhappy, means: You had known me the answer in the past.
19:5: He says: And I feared my cousins and my clan after me? He says: After me, that they would inherit me. It was said: What he meant by his saying behind me is in front of me and in front of me. I have explained the permissibility of that previously. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And I feared the relatives after me, meaning by the relatives: the relatives who are not related to him, that they would inherit him, so God gave him Yahya. Yahya bin Dawud Al-Wasiti told us: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement, And I feared my relatives after me, he said: The clan. Abu Kuraib told us: Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement, And I feared my relatives after me, he said: He feared my relatives who were not related to me. Mujahid bin Musa told us: Yazid told us: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Abu Saleh, something similar. Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, And I feared the relatives after me, he said: He means the kalalah. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, I feared my relatives behind me, he said: The clan. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Indeed, I feared my relatives after me, he said: the clan. Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And I feared the loyalists after me. Purify. The loyalists are the clan, and the loyalists are the plural of mawla, and the loyalist and the guardian in the speech of the Arabs are one and the same. The reading of the regions is And I feared the loyalists meaning: the fear that is the opposite of security. It was narrated on the authority of Uthman bin Affan that he read it: And I feared the loyalists with a shaddah on the fa and a fathah on the kha from the lightness, as if the interpretation of the statement is: And my clan is gone and who will inherit me from my paternal uncles. And if it is read in this way, the ya’ of the loyalists is silent and not moving, because it is in the place of raising with a lightness. And his saying, And my wife was barren, means: And my wife was not giving birth. It is said from this: a barren man, and a barren woman with the same word, as the poet said: What a bad young man I am if I am blind, barren, and a coward. What excuse do I have before every witness? His saying, Then grant me from Yourself a protector, means: So grant me from Yourself a son who will inherit and help.
19:6: And his saying, He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, means: He will inherit my money after my death, and he will inherit from the family of Jacob the prophecy, because Zachariah was from the descendants of Jacob. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement, He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, meaning: He will inherit my money and inherit from the family of Jacob the prophecy. Mujahid told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Ismail told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement, He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, he said: He will inherit my money, and he will inherit from the family of Jacob the prophethood. Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement, He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, he said: He will inherit my money, and he will inherit from the family of Jacob the prophecy. Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement, He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Yaqub, he said: He will be a prophet just as his fathers were prophets. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, He will inherit from me and inherit from the family of Jacob. He said: And his inheritance was a knowledge, and Zakariya was from the descendants of Jacob. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: His inheritance was knowledge, and Zakariya was from the descendants of Jacob. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement, He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, he said: His prophethood and his knowledge. Abu Kuraib told us: Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God have mercy on my brother Zachariah, for what he did to the heirs of his wealth when he said: So grant me from Yourself an heir who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, he said: Al-Hasan used to say: He will inherit his prophethood and his knowledge. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that when the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse and came to He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, he would say: May God have mercy on Zachariah for what he had from his heirs. Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God have mercy on Zachariah and what happened to his heirs? And may God have mercy on Lot, for he used to take refuge in a strong pillar. Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, Then grant me from Yourself an heir * Who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob. He said: He will inherit my prophethood and the prophethood of the family of Jacob. The reciters differed in their reading of the statement, He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob. The reciters of Medina and Mecca and a group of the people of Kufa read it as He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, raising both letters. Meaning: So grant the one who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, on the condition that he will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, from the connection of the guardian. A group of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it as He will inherit me and inherit, with the two letters in the subjunctive mood as a condition, meaning: So grant me from Yourself a guardian, for he will inherit me if You grant him to me. Those who read it like this said: It is only appropriate in this place, because He will inherit me is from a verse other than the one before it. They said: It is only appropriate for something like this to be a connection, if it is not disconnected from what it is connected to, like His statement, A support that will support me. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two readings in my opinion is the reading of the one who reads it with the two letters raised as a connection to the guardian, because the guardian is indefinite, and that Zachariah only asked his Lord to grant him a guardian who would have this description, as was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, not that he asked Him for a guardian, then he informed that if He granted him that, this would be his description, because if that were the case, that would be from Zachariah entering into the knowledge of the unseen which God has concealed from His creation. And his saying, And make him, O Lord, pleasing, means: And make, O Lord, the guardian whom You grant me pleasing, pleasing to You and to Your servants with his pleasure in religion, character, and morals. And pleasing is a verbal noun inflected from the object of the verb.
19:7: God Almighty says: So his Lord responded to him and said to him: O Zachariah, indeed We give you good tidings of Our grant to you of a boy whose name will be John. Qatada used to say: God named him John because He brought him back to life through faith. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying, O Zachariah, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be John, a servant whom God brought to life for faith. And his saying, We have not made for him before any namesake, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of that. Some of them said: Its meaning is that no barren woman has ever given birth to anyone like him. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying to Yahya, We have not made for him a namesake before, means: barren women have never given birth to a child like him. Others said: Rather, its meaning is: We did not make for him an example before him. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Al-Rabi’ told us: Salim bin Qutaybah told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, We have not made for Him any namesake before, he said: any similar. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, We have not made for him before any namesake, he said: An example. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Others said: This means that no one was named after him before him. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, We have not made for him a namesake before, no one had been named with that name before him. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, We have not made for him a namesake before, he said: No one was named Yahya before him. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, the same. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam told us regarding the statement of God, We have not made for him any namesake before, he said: No one before him was named with this name. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: “Indeed, We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be Yahya. We have not given anyone before him a namesake.” No one before him was named Yahya. Abu Ja`far said: This statement, I mean the statement of the one who said: There was no one before Yahya named after him for Yahya, is more similar to the interpretation of that, and the meaning of the statement is: We did not make for the boy whom we gave as a spoil to you, whose name was Yahya before him, anyone named after him, and the word named is a noun derived from muf’il ilayhi.
19:8: God the Almighty says: Zachariah said when God gave him the good report of John: My Lord, how will I have a boy? And how can that be for me, while my wife is barren and cannot conceive, and I have become too weak from old age to have intercourse with women? Will You strengthen me to do what I have become too weak for, and make my wife fertile, for You are able to do that and to do what You will, or should I marry a wife other than my barren wife? He seeks confirmation from his Lord of the report, about the way in which the child that God gave him the good report would be for him, not out of denial from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the reality of what God promised him of a child, and how could that be a denial from him that He would grant him the child that He gave him the good report of, when he was the one who initiated the question to his Lord with His saying: Then grant me from Yourself an heir * Who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob after His saying: Indeed, my bones have weakened and my head is shining with white hair. Al-Saddī said about this: Musa bin Harun told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: Gabriel called to Zachariah, "Indeed, We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be John. We have not given anyone before a namesake." When he heard the call, Satan came to him and said: O Zachariah, the voice that you heard is not from God, it is rather from Satan mocking you. If it were from God, He would have revealed it to you as He reveals to you other matters. So he doubted and said: How can I have a boy? He said: Where can he be from? And I have reached old age and my wife is barren. His saying, And I have reached extreme old age, means: I have become extremely old and have become like dry bones. It is said of a dry stick: an extremely old and stubborn stick. It has become extremely old, ya’tiyan and ‘atwan, and ‘asa ya’su ‘asan and ‘aswan. Everyone who has reached his limit in arrogance, corruption, or disbelief is extremely old and stubborn. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Husayn told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: I have learned the entire Sunnah, except that I do not know whether the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite in the noon and afternoon prayers or not, and I do not know how he used to recite this letter and I have reached extreme old age or deep old age. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And I have reached extreme old age, he said: By extreme old age he means old age. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement atiya he said: thinness of bone. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, from old age, insolence, he said: in age, and he was seventy-something years old. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And I have reached extreme old age, he said: The one who has become too old to have children is someone who thinks he will never have children. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And I have reached extreme old age, that it is old age.
19:9: God Almighty says: God said to Zachariah, answering him, He said, ‘Likewise.’ He says: This is the matter, as you say that your wife is barren, and that you have reached extreme old age. But your Lord says: The creation of what you gave me good report of, the boy whose name I told you was John, is easy for Me. So, from His saying, Your Lord said, ‘It is easy for Me.’ He is a metaphor for creation. And His statement, And I created you before, and you were nothing, the Most High says, “The creation of what I promised you that I would give you of the boy whose matter I mentioned to you since your old age and the barrenness of your wife is not more wondrous than your creation, for I created you and brought you into being a sound human being before My creation, and I did not give you the good report that I would give you of a child, and you were nothing, so likewise will I create for you the child that I gave you the good report of from your barren wife, with your old age and the weakness of your bones and the white hair of your head.”
19:10: And His saying, He said, ‘My Lord, make for me a sign.’ God Almighty says: Zachariah said: O Lord, make for me a sign and proof of what Your angels gave me of this boy about Your command and Your message, so that my heart may be reassured by that. As Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, He said, ‘My Lord, make for me a sign,’ he said: He said, My Lord, make for me a sign that this is from You. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: He said: O Lord, if this voice is from you, then make for me a sign. God said: Your sign for that is that you will not speak to people for three nights while you are sound and healthy. There is no illness or disease preventing you from speaking. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Three nights together. He said: His tongue was tied without illness. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying three nights together means: without being mute. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, three nights together, he said: Do not let illness prevent you from speaking. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, That you do not speak to people for three nights in a row. He said: Healthy, and illness does not prevent you from speaking. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, “He said: Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three nights, without harm or muteness. He was only punished with that because he asked for a sign after the angels had spoken to him face to face, and he took hold of his tongue until he could not speak without nodding. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, “three nights together,” he said: together, without being mute. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, He said, ‘Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three nights,’ and you are healthy. He said: So his tongue was tied, and he was unable to speak to anyone, and in that time he would glorify God, read the Torah, and read the Gospel. But if he wanted to speak to people, he was unable to speak to them. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who said: God took hold of his tongue without harm, so he could no longer speak, and he only spoke to his people by gesture, until the three days had passed which God made a sign to fulfill what He promised him of His gift to him. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, “He said: Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three nights, without being mute except by gestures.” So his tongue was tied for three days and three nights. Others said: Al-Sawi is an attribute of days. They said: The meaning of the speech is: He said, Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three consecutive nights. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, He said, Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three consecutive nights. He said: Three consecutive nights.
19:11: God Almighty says: Then Zachariah came out to his people from his place of prayer when he had restrained his tongue from speaking to the people, as a sign from God to him of the truth of His promise to him. Ibn Jurayj used to say about the meaning of his exit from his prayer niche: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, So he came out to his people from the prayer niche. He said: He looked out over his people from the prayer niche. Abu Jaafar said: We have explained the meaning of the mihrab before, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, So he came out to his people from the sanctuary, he said: The sanctuary is his place of prayer, and he read, Then the angels called to him while he was standing praying in the sanctuary. And his saying, Then He revealed to them, means: He pointed to them. And that signal may be with the hand, with a book, or something else, by which one understands what he wants. And the Arabs have two dialects for that: waha revelation and awha inspiration. So whoever says waha revelation, says in yaf’al he does yahy he gives life, and whoever says awha revelation, says yuhy he inspires, and likewise awma gesture and yawma gesture. So whoever says wama gesture, says in yaf’al he does yamy he gives life, and whoever says awma gesture, says yawmi my day. The interpreters differed about the meaning by which he revealed to his people. Some of them said: He revealed to them by a gesture with his hand. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, So He revealed: So Zakariya pointed. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih: Then He revealed to them. He said: Revelation is a sign. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: So he revealed to them, he said: He gestured to them. Others said: The meaning of inspired is wrote. Who said that? Mahmoud bin Khidash told us: Ibad bin Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Sufyan bin Hussein, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty: Then He inspired them to glorify Him morning and evening, he said: It was written for them on the earth. Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of al-Hakam: Then He revealed to them. He said: He wrote to them. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, So he came out to his people from the sanctuary, and he wrote for them in a book, that they should glorify God morning and evening, and that is his saying, So he inspired them. Others said: The meaning of this is: their command. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Then He inspired them to glorify Him morning and evening, he said: I do not know whether it was a book that He wrote for them, or a sign that He indicated, and God knows best. He said: He commanded them to glorify Him morning and evening, and He did not speak to them. His saying, That they glorify Him in the morning and the evening, has been explained previously in the ways in which glorification is directed. It may be possible in this place that he meant by it glorification, which is the remembrance of God, so their command to devote themselves to the remembrance of God at the two ends of the day by glorifying Him. It may also be possible that he meant by it prayer, so their command to pray at these two times. Qatada used to say about this: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Then He inspired them to glorify Him in the morning and the evening. He said: He signaled to them to pray in the morning and the evening.
19:12: God Almighty says: Then John was born to Zachariah. When he was born, God said to him: O John, take this book with strength, meaning the book of God that He revealed to Moses, which is the Torah. With strength, he says: with seriousness. As Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Take the Book with strength, he said: Seriously. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Take the Book with strength, he said: seriously. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Zayd said about this: Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, O Yahya, take the Book with strength, he said: Strength is to do what God has commanded him to do and to avoid what God has forbidden him to do. Abu Jaafar said: I have explained the meaning of that with its evidence in what has passed in this book of ours, in Surat Al Imran, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And His statement, And We gave him judgment while he was a boy, means that God Almighty says: And We gave him understanding of the Book of God while he was a boy, before he reached the age of manhood. Ahmad bin Mani’ told us: Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us: Muammar told me, and he did not mention it from anyone else regarding this verse: And We gave him judgment while he was a boy. He said: It reached me that the boys said to Yahya: Let us go play. He said: I was not created for play. So God revealed: And We gave him judgment while he was a boy.
19:13: And His saying, And mercy from Us, God Almighty says: And mercy from Us and love for him, We gave him wisdom while he was a boy. The interpreters differed about the meaning of compassion. Some of them said: It means mercy, and they directed the speech to something similar to the meaning we directed it to. Who said that? Ali told us, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And compassion from Us, meaning: And mercy from Us. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of `Ikrimah, regarding this verse, And compassion from Us, he said: Mercy. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And compassion from Us, he said: Mercy from Us. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, his statement: And compassion from Us he said: Mercy from Us, and no one possesses the power to bestow it except Us. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And compassion from Us, meaning: Mercy from Us, which no one other than Us is able to give. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And a mercy from Us to Zachariah. We gave him wisdom while he was a boy, and We did to him what We did. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And compassion from Us, meaning: mercy from Us. Others said: The meaning of this is: Out of compassion for him, we did that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us? And Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, And compassion from Us, he said: compassion from his Lord towards him. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Others said: Rather, the meaning of compassion is love. They directed the meaning of the words to: And out of love from Us, We did that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Ikrimah: And compassion from Us. He said: Love for him. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, and compassion, he said: As for compassion, it is love. Others said that it means that we respect him. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Rabah, And compassion from Us. He said: Exaltation from Us. It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he said: I do not know what compassion is. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Amr ibn Dinar told me that he heard Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: By God, I do not know what Hanan is. And the Arabs have two dialects for Hananak: Hananak, O our Lord, and Hananaik? As Tarafa ibn al-Abd said about Hananaik: Abu Munther, you have perished, so let some of us outlast your kindness. Some evil is less serious than others. Imru Al-Qais said in another language: And the Banu Shamji bin Jarim give it to their goat, your compassion, the compassionate one. The Arab scholars differed about Hananik. Some of them said: It is the dual of Hanan. Others said: Rather, it is a language that is not a dual. They said: That is like their saying: Hawalik? And as the poet said: Hitting, stabbing and shaking Those who said that Hananik is a dual have equated all of that, in that all of it is a dual. The origin of that, I mean Hanan, is from the saying of the speaker: So-and-so yearned for such-and-such, meaning he felt comfortable with him and longed for him. Then it is said: So-and-so yearned for so-and-so, if he described himself as being affectionate towards him, tender towards him, and merciful towards him, as the poet said: Have mercy on that king, for every situation has its own words. Meaning: Be kind to me. Tenderness: is a noun derived from the saying: Welcome so-and-so to so-and-so. It is said from this: I was kind to him, so I am kind to him with tenderness and affection. From this, it is said of a man’s wife: He was kind to him, because he was kind to her and showed her affection, as the rajaz poet said: And one dark night I walked, and Hannah and Beit did not harm me. And His saying, and zakat, God Almighty says: And We gave Yahya wisdom while he was a boy, and zakat: which is purification from sins, and using his body in the obedience of his Lord, so zakat is in apposition to wisdom from His saying, And We gave him wisdom. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement and zakat he said: Zakat is righteous work. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement, and zakat, he said: righteous, pure work. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, and zakat, meaning righteous, pure deeds. And His saying, And he was pious, God Almighty says: And he was fearful of God, performing His obligations, avoiding His prohibitions, and hastening to obey Him. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And he paid zakat and was pious. He said: He was pure and did not commit a sin. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, and zakat, and he was righteous, he said: As for zakat and piety, people have known them.
19:14: God Almighty says: He was dutiful to his parents, quick to obey them and love them, not disobedient to them. And he was not a disobedient tyrant. God Almighty says: He was not arrogant about obeying his Lord and obeying his parents, but he was humble and submissive to God and his parents, obeying what He commanded and refraining from what He forbade, not disobeying his Lord or his parents. His saying disobedient is a noun meaning that he is disobedient, from the saying of the speaker: So-and-so disobeyed his Lord, so he disobeys Him disobediently.
19:15: And his saying, "Peace be upon him the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive," means: And security from God the day he was born, from Satan afflicting him with evil, as he afflicts the children of Adam, and that is because it was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Every child of Adam will come on the Day of Resurrection with a sin except for what was from John, son of Zechariah. Ibn Hamid told us that: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yahya ibn Saeed, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Ibn al-Aas told me that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say that. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, a disobedient tyrant, he said: Ibn al-Musayyab used to mention that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No one will meet God on the Day of Resurrection except one who has sinned, except Yahya ibn Zakariya. He said: Qatada said: He did not sin, nor did he intend to have intercourse with a woman. And his saying, And on the Day he dies, he says: And security from God Almighty for him from the trials of the grave, and from the terror of the Day of Resurrection. And on the Day he is raised alive, he says: And security for him from the punishment of God on the Day of Resurrection, the Day of the Greatest Terror, from anything terrifying him, or from what terrifies creation. It was mentioned about Ibn Uyaynah in this regard: Ahmad bin Mansour Al-Fayrozi told me: Sadaqah bin Al-Fadl told me: I heard Ibn Atiyah say: The most frightening thing for a person is in three situations: the day he is born and sees himself emerging from what he was in; the day he dies and sees a people he has never seen; and the day he is resurrected and sees himself in a great gathering place. He said: So God honored Yahya bin Zakariya in it, and singled him out with peace, saying: “And peace be upon him the day he was born and the day he dies and the day he is resurrected alive.” Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, that Al-Hasan said: Jesus and John met, and Jesus said to him: Ask forgiveness for me, you are better than me. The other said to him: Ask forgiveness for me, you are better than me. Jesus said to him: You are better than me. Have you greeted myself? And may God greet you. So God recognized its virtue.
19:16: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And remember, O Muhammad, in the Book of God which He revealed to you in truth, Mary, the daughter of Imran, when she withdrew from her family and separated herself from them. It is derived from the verb nabdh, and nabdh means throwing away, and we have explained that with its evidence previously. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And mention in the Book, Mary, when she withdrew, meaning she was isolated from her family. Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When she withdrew from her people to a place in the east. He said: She went out to a place in the east. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: Mary went out to the side of the prayer niche because of her menses, and this is His statement: Then she withdrew from her family to a place to the east: to the east of the prayer niche. And his saying, an eastern place, means: So she moved away and isolated herself from her people in a place before the rising of the sun, not its setting. As Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, an eastern place, he said: from the east. Ishaq bin Shaheen told me: Khalid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I know God’s creation, why did the Christians take the east as their qiblah? Because God said: Then she withdrew from her people to a place in the east, so they took the birth of Jesus as their qiblah. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The People of the Book were prescribed to pray towards the House and to perform the Hajj for God, and nothing turned them away from them except that your Lord said: You have withdrawn from your people to a place in the East, so they prayed before sunrise. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, When she withdrew from her people to a place to the east. He said: Vast and secluded. It was said: It only became a place near the rising of the sun, because what was near the east was better for them than what was near the west, and that is also what was mentioned among the Arabs.
19:17: And his saying, So she took a veil from them means: So she took a veil from her family to conceal her from them and from the people. And it was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas that she was in a place facing the east, because God shaded her with the sun and made a veil from it for her. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, She withdrew from her people to a place to the east, he said: A place where the sun shaded her so that none of them could see her. Another said about this: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: So I took a veil from them of walls. And His saying, So We sent to her Our Spirit, means that God Almighty says: So We sent to her when she withdrew from her people to a place in the east, and took a veil from them: Gabriel. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Then We sent to her Our spirit, he said: Gabriel was sent to her, as he told us. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: I found Gabriel with her, whom God had represented as a perfect human being. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement, Then We sent to her Our spirit, he said: Gabriel. Muhammad bin Sahl told me: Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us: Abdul Samad bin Maqal, the nephew of Wahb, told me: I heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: God sent Gabriel to Mary, and he appeared to her as a perfect human being. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said: When she had purified herself, meaning Mary from her menstruation, there was a man with her, and this is His statement: Then We sent to her Our Spirit, and he appeared to her as a well-proportioned man. God Almighty says: So he appeared to her in the form of a human being of sound creation among them, meaning in the form of a man from the children of Adam, of moderate creation.
19:18: God Almighty says: Mary feared Our Messenger, when he appeared to her as a well-mannered man, and she thought he was a man who wanted to have intercourse with her. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement, Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Gracious from you, if you should be fearing God. He said: I feared that he only wanted it for herself. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, Then he appeared to her as a well-proportioned man. When she saw him, she was terrified by him and said: I seek refuge in the Most Gracious from you, if you should fear God. So she said: I seek refuge, O man, in the Most Gracious from you. She said: I seek refuge in the Most Gracious from you lest you do to me what He has forbidden you, if you have piety towards Him, fear His prohibitions, and avoid His disobedience, because whoever fears God, then he avoids that. If this was interpreted to mean: I seek refuge in the Most Gracious from you, if you fear God in my seeking refuge and protection in Him from you, then that would be correct. Ibn Hamid also told us, saying: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, She said, ‘I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be righteous.’ And you do not see anything but that he is a man from the children of Adam.
19:19: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Asim, he said: Ibn Zayd said: And he mentioned the stories of Mary and said: You know that the pious one has a mind when she said: Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be fearing God. He said: I am only a messenger from your Lord. God Almighty says: Then Our Spirit said to her: "I am only a messenger from your Lord, O Mary. He sent me to you "to give you a pure boy." The reciters differed in reading this. The reciters of Hijaz and Iraq, other than Abu Amr, read it as laahbi lak meaning: I am only a messenger from your Lord. He said: He sent me to you to give you a pure boy in the narrative. Abu Amr bin Al-Ala read it as liahbi lak ghulam zakiyyan meaning: I am only a messenger from your Lord. He sent me to you so that God may give you a pure boy. Abu Ja`far said: The correct reading in this regard is what the reciters of the regions have said, which is la-ahba laka with an alif without a ya’, because this is how it is in the copies of the Qur’an of the Muslims, and this is the reading of their ancients and moderns, except for Abu `Amr, and it is not permissible to differ from them in what they have agreed upon, and it is not permissible for anyone to differ from their copies of the Qur’an. The pure boy is the one who is pure from sins, and the Arabs also say: a pure and virtuous boy, and a high and high boy.
19:20: God Almighty says: Mary said to Gabriel, How can I have a boy? How can I have a boy? Is it before a husband that I marry, so that I may provide for him from him, or does God begin his creation from the beginning? And no man has touched me from the children of Adam through lawful marriage nor have I since none of them touched me in a lawful way out of lust I desired and did that in an unlawful way, so I conceived him from fornication. As Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, And I was not a prostitute, meaning: a fornicator.
19:21: He said, 'Thus said your Lord, it is easy for Me.' God Almighty says: Gabriel said to her: "This is the matter as you describe, that no man has touched you and you are not unchaste, but your Lord said: It is easy for Me." That is, creating the boy whom you said I would give you is easy for Me, and it is not difficult for Me to create him. I gave him to you without a male to conquer you. And We will make him a sign to the people. He says: And so that We may make the boy whom We give to you a sign and proof of My creation, I give him to you. And a mercy from Us. He says: And a mercy from Us to you, and to whoever believes in him and acknowledges him, I create him from you. And it was a matter already decreed. He says: And his creation from you was a matter that God had decreed, and His judgment had gone ahead, and His foreknowledge preceded that he would be from you. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Someone I do not accuse told me, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih: And it was a matter decreed, meaning that God had decided on it, so there was no escape from it.
19:22: In this speech there is something that was omitted, its mention was omitted, as the indication of what was mentioned of it was sufficient for it. So We breathed into him of Our spirit into a boy. And she carried him and withdrew with him to a remote place. And thus came the interpretation of the people of interpretation. Who said that? Muhammad bin Sahl told me, he said: Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, he said: Abdul Samad bin Maqal, the nephew of Wahb bin Munabbih, said: I heard Wahb say: When God sent Gabriel to Mary, he appeared to her as a perfect human being, and she said to him, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be righteous. Then he blew into the pocket of her garment until the breath reached the womb and it was covered. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who said: When he said that, meaning when Gabriel said, “Thus says your Lord: it is easy for Me,” the verse, she submitted to God’s command, so He blew into her bosom and then left her. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said: She threw her jilbab over her when Gabriel said that to her, so Gabriel took hold of her sleeves and blew into the pocket of her robe, which was torn in the front, and the breath entered her chest, and she became pregnant. Then her sister, the wife of Zachariah, came to visit her one night, and when she opened the door for her, she embraced her, and the wife of Zachariah said: O Mary, do you perceive that I am pregnant? Mary said: I also perceive that I am pregnant. The wife of Zachariah said: I have found that which is in my womb prostrating to that which is in your womb. So that is his saying, Confirming a word from God. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: They say: He only blew into the pocket of her armor and her sleeve. And his saying, So I withdrew with him to a remote place, means: So I isolated myself with the one I carried, who was Jesus, and I withdrew with him to a remote place from the people. He says: A place far away from the people. It is said: He is in a remote place and Qasaf has the same meaning, as the rajaz poet said: You will sit in the seat far away from me, you dirty, fried one It is said: The place became distant, and I distanced the thing: if I removed it and delayed it. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, So she withdrew with him to a remote place, he said: A remote place. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, a remote place, he said: remote. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: When it was time for Mary to give birth, she went out to the eastern side of the prayer niche and reached its farthest point.
19:23: And His saying, So the birth pangs brought her to the trunk of the palm tree, the Most High says: So the birth pangs brought her to the trunk of the palm tree, then it was said: When the ba' was dropped from it, it brought her, just as it is said: I brought you Zayd, so if the ba' is deleted, it is said: I brought you Zayd, just as the Most High said: Bring me iron sheets, and the meaning is: Bring me iron sheets, but the alif was extended when the ba' was deleted, and just as they said: I went out with it and I brought it out, and I went with it and I made it go, and it is more effective than coming, just as it is said: He came, and I brought him, meaning I brought him, and an example of the Arabs: The worst that came to me is the brain of Achilles tendon, and I willed, and it is said: The worst that comes to you and wills you to that, and from it is the saying of Zuhair: A neighbor who came to you relying on you, fear and hope came to him Meaning: He brought it, and he brought it to us, and he made you happy: from the language of Tamim, and he brought you from the language of the people of Aliyah, and the one who interpreted that interpreted it to mean: he forced her, because when the labor pains came to her at the trunk of the palm tree, he had forced her to it. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, Then the birth pangs came upon her, he said: The birth pangs forced her to labor. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The birth pangs forced her to go to the trunk of the palm tree. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: The birth pangs forced her to go to the trunk of the palm tree. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Then the birth pangs drove her to the trunk of the palm tree. He said: The birth pangs forced her to the trunk of the palm tree. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Then the pangs of childbirth drove her to the trunk of the palm tree, he said: He forced her to the trunk of the palm tree. They differed as to the place where Mary took Jesus to give birth and where the labor pains came to her. Some of them said: It was in the lowest part of Egypt and the last part of Syria. This is because she fled from her people when she became pregnant, so she headed towards Egypt, fleeing from them. Who said that? Muhammad bin Sahl told us: Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us: Abdul Samad bin Maqal told us that he heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: When Mary became pregnant, there was with her a relative of hers called Yusuf the carpenter. They were going to the mosque near Mount Zion, and that mosque at that time was one of their greatest mosques. Mary and Yusuf were serving in that mosque at that time, and there was great merit in serving it, so they desired that, so they were in charge of treating it themselves, cleaning it, sweeping it, purifying it, and every work that was done in it. No one among the people of their time worked more diligently and worshipped than them. The first to deny Mary’s pregnancy was her companion Yusuf. When he saw what was wrong with her, he was horrified by it, and it was great and terrible for him, so he did not know what to base his case on. When Yusuf wanted to accuse her, he mentioned her righteousness and innocence, and that she had never been away from him for a single hour. When he wanted to acquit her, he saw what had appeared on her. When that became too much for him, he spoke to her, and the first thing he said to her was: He said to her: Something has occurred to me about you that I feared, and I was keen to conceal it and keep it to myself, but that overcame me, and I found that speaking about it would be more healing for my chest. She said: Then say something nice. He said: “I would not say anything to you except that, so tell me. Can a plant grow without a seed?” She said: Yes. He said: Can a tree grow without rain falling on it? She said: Yes. He said: Can there be a boy without a boy? She said: Yes. He said: “Do you not know that God, the Blessed and Exalted, caused the plant to grow on the day He created it without a seed, and that the seed on that day only came from the plant that God caused to grow without a seed? Or do you not know that God, by His power, caused the tree to grow without rain, and that by that power He made the rain life for the tree after He created each one of them alone?” Or do you say: God will not be able to cause the tree to grow until He seeks help from water, and were it not for that He would not have been able to cause it to grow? Joseph said to her: I do not say this, but I know that God Almighty has power over whatever He wills. He says to it, Be, and it is. Mary said: Did you not know that God Almighty created Adam and his wife without a female or a male? He said: Yes. So when she told him that, it occurred to him that what was in her was something from God Almighty, and that he could not ask her about it, because he saw that she was concealing it. Then Joseph took over the service of the mosque, and he spared her all the work she used to do there, because he saw the delicacy of her body, the yellowness of her color, the ageing of her face, the protrusion of her belly, the weakness of her strength, and the narrowness of her sight. Mary had not been like that before, so when her period of confinement approached, God revealed to her, Leave the land of your people, for if they get hold of you, they will insult you and kill your son. So she confided that to her sister, and her sister was pregnant at that time, and she had been given the good report of Yahya. When they met, Yahya’s mother found what was in her womb falling on its face, prostrating herself, confessing to Jesus. So Joseph carried her to the land of Egypt on his donkey, with nothing between it and the saddlebags when she rode. So Joseph set out with her until he was adjacent to the land of Egypt, at the farthest reaches of her people’s land. Mary was in confinement, and he forced her to the donkey’s manger, meaning the donkey’s trough, and the base of a palm tree. That was at a time when I think it was cold or hot, Abu Ja’far was skeptical, so Mary was distressed. The labor pains were severe, so she took refuge in a palm tree and embraced it, and the angels surrounded her, standing in rows surrounding her. Another statement other than this was narrated on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, which is: Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When the time for her Mary’s delivery was approaching, and she experienced what a woman experiences in labor pains, she left the city, heading west from Ilia, until the birth overtook her at a village six miles from Ilia called Bethlehem. Then the labor pains brought her to the base of a palm tree, where there was a cow’s manger and beneath it a spring of water, so she gave birth to him near it. Others said: Rather, when the time came for her to give birth, she went out to the eastern side of the prayer niche, and she came to its farthest point, and the labor pains forced her to the trunk of the palm tree. This is what al-Suddi said, and the narration of it was mentioned before. Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me: Hajjaj told us: Ibn Jurayj said: Al-Mughira bin Othman told me: I heard Ibn Abbas say: It was not long before she became pregnant and gave birth. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: And Al-Mughira bin Othman bin Abdullah informed me that he heard Ibn Abbas say: It is not until she became pregnant and gave birth. And his saying, I wish I had died before this, he mentioned that she said that during labor out of shyness in front of people. As Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: She said while she was being released from the rope out of shyness from the al-Nas 114:Oh, I wish I had died before this distress that I am in, and the grief of giving birth to a child without a husband, and I had been forgotten. She says: Oh, I wish I had died before this distress that I am in, and the grief of giving birth to a child without a husband, and I had been forgotten: something that was forgotten and then not sought after, like menstrual rags that when they are thrown away and discarded are not sought after or mentioned. Likewise, everything that is forgotten and left and not sought after is forgotten. And forgotten with the opening of the letter noon and its breaking are two well-known dialects of the Arabic languages with the same meaning, like the string and the string, and the bridge and the bridge, and whichever of them the reader recites is correct in our view, and with the breaking the majority of the readers of Hijaz, Madinah, and Basra and some of the people of Kufa recited it, and with the opening it is recited by the people of Kufa, and from it the saying of the poet: As if she has forgotten about the earth, she tells it when she comes out, and if she talks to you, she is noble. What he means by his saying: she sought it is: she sought it, because she had forgotten it until it was lost, then she remembered it and sought it. What he means by his saying: she sought it is: she did good and was truthful. If the word forget had been directed to the source of forgetfulness, it would have been correct. This is because the Arabs, as mentioned about them, say: I forgot it by forgetfulness and forgetfulness, as some of them said from the obedience of the Lord and the disobedience of Satan, meaning and disobedience, and as you say I came to it by coming and coming, as the poet said: They are known for their immoral acts and consider doing good deeds as forbidden. His saying forgotten is an action verb from I forgot something, as if she said: I wish I were the thing that was thrown away, then left and forgotten. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ata’ Al-Khurasani told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying, Oh, I wish I had died before this and was forgotten and forgotten, I was not created, and I was nothing. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, And I was forgotten, forgotten. He says: forgotten: my memory was forgotten, and forgotten: you say: my trace was forgotten, so no trace or eye can see me. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And I was forgotten and forgotten: meaning something that is not known or remembered. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And I was forgotten, forgotten, he said: I do not know and it is not known who I am. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Anas, Forgotten he said: It is the miscarriage. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, Oh, I wish I had died before this and was forgotten and forgotten, I was never anything on earth.
19:24: The reciters differed in reading this, so most of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as Fanaddaha min tahtaha meaning: Gabriel called her from in front of her, although they differed in their interpretation of it. Some of them interpreted it as min tahtaha in this way, and some of them interpreted it as Jesus, and that he called her from beneath her after she gave birth to him. Some of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it as Fanaddaha min tahtaha with the opening of the two ta's from below, meaning: The one beneath her called her, on the basis that the one beneath her was Jesus, and that he was the one who called his mother. It was mentioned that he said: The one who called her from beneath her was the king. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Abdul-Mumin told us: I heard Ibn Abbas read: And he called to her from beneath her, meaning: Gabriel. Ahmad bin Abdullah Ahmad bin Yunus told me: Abthar told us: Hisin told us, on the authority of Amr bin Maimun Al-Awdi: Al-Razi called out to her, the king. Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, that he read: So he addressed her from beneath her. Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us: Yahya told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, that he recited: So he addressed her from beneath her. Al-Rafa’i told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, that he read it in this way. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Amer told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, He called to her from beneath her, he said: Gabriel. Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: He called to her from beneath her: meaning from beneath the palm tree. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Then Gabriel called to her from beneath her, ‘Do not grieve.’ Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Then he called to her from beneath her, he said: The angel. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And he called to her from beneath her, meaning: Gabriel was below her. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, He called to her from beneath her, he said: Gabriel called to her and Jesus did not speak until she came to her people. Mention of those who said: Jesus, peace be upon him, called her. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, And he called to her from beneath her, he said: Jesus, son of Mary.
