Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Amer told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And he called to her from beneath her - her son. Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Al-Hasan said: He is her son. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih: Then Jesus called to her from beneath her, ‘Do not grieve.’ Abu Hamid Ahmad bin Al-Mughira Al-Himsi told me: Uthman bin Saeed told us: Muhammad bin Muhajir told us, on the authority of Thabit bin Ajlan, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement, So he called to her from beneath her, Isa said: Do you not hear God say, So she pointed to him. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: Then he called to her from beneath her. Jesus said: He called to her: Do not grieve, your Lord has provided a stream beneath you. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah Al-Riyahi, on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b, who said: The one who spoke to her was the one she carried in her womb and who entered her mouth. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two opinions in this regard, in our view, is the opinion of those who said: The one who called her was her son Jesus. This is because it is a metaphor for mentioning him closer to him than mentioning Gabriel, so referring him to the one who is closer to him is more appropriate than referring him to the one who is further away from him. Do you not see in the context of his statement, So she carried him and withdrew with him to a remote place, meaning: So she carried Jesus and withdrew with him. Then it was said: So he called her, in sequence with that of mentioning Jesus and reporting about him. And another reason is his saying, So she pointed to him, and she did not point to him, God willing, except when she knew that he was speaking in that state, and because of what she had known and trusted from him by his addressing her with his saying to her, Do not grieve, your Lord has provided a stream beneath you, and what God informed about him, that he said to her, Point to him to the people, and if that had been a saying from Gabriel, it would have been appropriate for it to be in the apparent meaning of the report, indicating that Jesus would speak and argue on her behalf for the people, and it was an order from him for her to point to him to the people if they asked her about her condition and his condition. If this is the correct interpretation that we have explained, then it is clear that both readings, I mean from beneath her with a kasra, and from beneath her with a fatha, are correct. This is because if it is read with a kasra, then in his saying then he called to her there is a mention of Jesus. And if it is read from beneath her with a fatha, then the action is for whom, which is Jesus. So the interpretation of the statement then is: then the newborn called to her from beneath her, Do not grieve, O mother. “Your Lord has provided a stream beneath you.” Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Then he called to her from beneath her, ‘Do not grieve,’ she said: How can I not grieve when you are with me, neither a husband so I can say who is my husband, nor a slave woman so I can say who is my master? Is there anything that would excuse me before the people? I wish I had died before this and was forgotten and forgotten, so Jesus said to her: I will suffice you in speaking. The people of interpretation differed about the one who was abused by the secret in this place. Some of them said: He meant by it: the small river. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Asim told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib: Your Lord has made a stream flow beneath you. He said: The stream. Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Al-Bara’ say about this verse, Your Lord has provided a stream beneath you. He said: The stream. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying, Your Lord has made a stream flow beneath you, which is the River Jesus. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Your Lord has made a stream flow beneath you. He said: The stream is the river that was under Mary when she gave birth to him. It was called a stream. Abu Hasin told me, he said: Abthar told us, he said: Hasin told us, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun Al-Awdi, he said regarding this verse, Your Lord has made a stream flow beneath you, he said: The stream is a river from which one drinks. Yaqub and Abu Kurayb told us: Hisham told us: Hisin told us, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun, regarding his statement, Your Lord has provided a stream beneath you, he said: It is a stream. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Sarya he said: a river in Syriac. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Ibn Jurayj said: A river next to it. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abu Dawud told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement, Your Lord has made a stream flow beneath you, he said: It was a stream, so Humayd bin Abd Al-Rahman said: The stream is the canal, so he said: The princes have overcome us in you. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, Your Lord has made a stream flow beneath you. He said: It is a stream, a small river, and in Nabataean it is: the secret. Abu Hamid Al-Himsi told me: Uthman bin Saeed told us: Muhammad bin Muhajir told us, on the authority of Thabit bin Ajlan, who said: I asked Saeed bin Jubair about Al-Sarri. He said: A river. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: The small river. Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Mughira told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, that he said: It is the small river, meaning the stream, meaning his saying, Your Lord has made a stream flow beneath you. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: A small stream in Syriac. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubaid bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Underneath you flows: a small stream from the rivers. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Your Lord has made a stream flow beneath you. The stream is the canal, which the people of Hijaz call it. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, regarding his statement a stream, he said: It is a stream. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone who is not accused, and on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih: Your Lord has made a stream flow beneath you, meaning a spring of water. Musa bin Harun told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Your Lord has made a stream flow beneath you. The stream is the river. Others said: He meant Jesus. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Your Lord has placed a stream beneath you. The stream is Jesus himself. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement, Your Lord has made a stream flow beneath you, meaning Himself. He said: And what is a stream flowing beneath it? He said: And those who say: The stream is the river, it is not like that, the river. If it were a river, it would only be beside it, and the river would not be beneath it. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two opinions on this, in my opinion, is that it was said that he meant the brook, and that is because he informed her of the water that God had given her, which He had placed near her, and said to her, “And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree, it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates. So eat” of these dates and drink of this water and be refreshed with your child. The stream is well-known in the speech of the Arabs as a small river, and from it is the saying of Labid: They were in the middle of the secret show and a crack in the wall, next to each other, their pens It is narrated: So we were imprisoned, and it is also narrated: So they left.
19:25: And his saying, And shake the trunk of the palm tree toward you, he mentioned that the trunk was a dry trunk, and he ordered her to shake it, and that was during the winter days, and shaking it was moving it. As Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement, And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree, he said: Move it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And shake the trunk of the palm tree toward you. He said: It was a dry trunk, so he said to it: Shake it, It will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Abdul-Mumin told us: I heard Abu Nahik say: It was a dry palm tree. Muhammad bin Sahl bin Askar told me: Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us: Abdul Samad bin Muqal told us: I heard Wahb bin Munabbih say about His statement, And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree, that the dates were falling on it, and that was in the winter. Musa bin Harun told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree. It was a trunk of it that had been cut off, so she shook it, and behold, it was a palm tree. A river was made to flow for it in the prayer niche, and the palm tree dropped fresh dates. So he said to it, Eat, drink, and be refreshed. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And shake the palm tree toward you. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, he said: Mujahid said: And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree. He said: The palm tree. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Isa bin Maimun, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree, he said: Ajwa dates. Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Husayn told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, that he recited this verse: And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree, it will drop upon you fresh, ripe dates. Amr said: There is nothing better for a woman in childbirth than dates and fresh dates. The preposition ba was inserted in His statement: And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree, just as one says: I have married you to so-and-so, or I have married you to so-and-so, and just as one says: It grows oil, meaning: It grows oil. The Arabs do this because actions are referred to by the preposition ba, so it is said when you refer to I struck Amr: I did it to him, and so on with every action. Therefore, the preposition ba is inserted in actions and is removed, so its entry and exit are one meaning, so the meaning of the statement is: And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree, and if the commentators had interpreted it in this way: And shake toward you fresh, ripe dates with the trunk of the palm tree, meaning: on the trunk of the palm tree, in a correct manner, but I do not remember anyone interpreting it in this way. And the evidence of the entry of the letter ba in the same place as its entry and exit is the poet’s saying: In Wadi Yaman, the lote tree grows at its top and bottom, with marakh and shabhan trees. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement tasaqtuqa dropped. The majority of the reciters of Medina, Basra and Kufa read it as tasaqtuqa with a ta’ from tasaqtuqa and with a shaddah on the seen, meaning: the palm tree drops upon you fresh, ripe dates. Then one of the two ta’s is assimilated into the other and is stressed. Those who read it in this way directed the meaning of the statement to: And shake the trunk of the palm tree toward you, the palm tree will drop upon you fresh dates. Some of the reciters of Kufa read it as tasaqtuqa with a ta’ and with a light seen, and directed the meaning of the statement to the same as those who stressed it directed it to, except that they differed with them in the reading. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin ‘Azib that he read it as yasaqtuqa with a ya’. Ahmad bin Yusuf told me that, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Yazid told us, on the authority of Jarir bin Hazim, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said: I heard Al-Bara’ bin Azib reciting it like that, and it was as if he directed the meaning of the speech to: And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree, and the trunk will drop upon you fresh, ripe dates. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Nahik that he used to read it as Taqatū with a damma on the ta’ and the omission of the alif. Ibn Hamid told us that: Yahya bin Wadh told us that Abdul-Mumin told us that he heard Abu Nahik recite it like that, and it was as if he directed the meaning of the speech to: The palm tree drops fresh dates on you. Abu Ja`far said: The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that these three readings, I mean tasaqtāt with a ta’ and a shaddah on the seen, with a ta’ and a light seen, and with a ya’ and a shaddah on the seen, are readings with similar meanings. Each of them has been read by readers who are knowledgeable about the Qur’an, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct in it. That is because if the trunk falls with its dates, and it is fixed and not cut off, then the palm tree has fallen with its dates. And if the palm tree falls with its dates, then the entire palm tree has fallen, its trunk and other than its trunk. That is because as long as the palm tree is standing on its foundation, it is only a trunk, a frond, and a palm branch. But if it is cut off, it becomes a trunk. So the trunk that Mary was ordered to shake, no one we know of has mentioned that it was a cut trunk other than al-Suddi. And it has been claimed that by shaking it it became a palm tree, so its meaning and the meaning of the one who said: The dates that fell on it were one palm tree, so the correctness of what we have said is clear. His saying harvested means harvested. Its original form was maf’ul, so it was changed to fa’il. The harvested is that which is taken fresh. Everything that is taken from a fruit, or transferred from its place with its freshness, has been harvested. Therefore it was said: So-and-so harvests truffles. From this comes the saying of Ibn Akht Jadhima: This is my crime and his choice in it, as every criminal has his hand in his mouth.
19:26: God the Most High says: So eat of the fresh dates that fall upon you, and drink of the gushing water which your Lord has placed beneath you, fear neither hunger nor thirst. And be refreshed means: And be content and rejoice at the birth of me and do not grieve. The ‘ayn is in the accusative case because it is the one described as settled. The meaning of the statement is: And let your eye be content with your child. Then the action was transferred from the ‘ayn to the woman who has the ‘ayn. So the ‘ayn was in the accusative case since the action was originally for her according to the interpretation, similar to what was done in His statement: But if they give up willingly to you anything thereof (An-Nisa’: 4), but it is: If they give up willingly to you anything thereof.” And His statement: And they are straitened with them (Hud 11:77- Al-‘Ankabut: 33). And from this is His statement: Fried fresh dates fall upon you meaning: Fried fresh dates fall upon you, so the action was transferred to the ‘ayn, according to the reading of those who read it with the letter ya’. In the reading of those who read it as tasaqat with a ta’, its meaning is: the dates of the palm tree fall on you, then the verb was changed to the palm tree. The reciters differed in their recitation of his statement wa-qari. As for the people of Medina, they recited it wa-qari with a fat-ha on the qaf, according to the language of those who say: I reqararat bi-makan, I reqara bi-hu, and I reqararat ‘ayn, I reqara bi-hu qurur. This is the language of Quraysh, as was mentioned to me, and the recitation is based on it. As for the people of Najd, they say: I reqararat bi-hu ‘ayn, I reqara bi-hu qarran, and I reqararat bi-hu, I reqara bi-hu, so the recitation is based on their language and wa-qari ‘ayn with a kasra on the qaf, and the recitation with us is based on the language of Quraysh with a fat-ha on the qaf. And His saying, If you see anyone from among mankind, means: If you see anyone from among the children of Adam speaking to you or asking you about something related to you and your child and the reason for his birth, then say, ‘Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast,’ meaning: So say: I have made it obligatory upon myself to God to be silent and not to speak to anyone from among the children of Adam today, so I will not speak to any human being today. And similar to what we said about the meaning of fasting, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say about this verse, Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, silence. Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, he said: Al-Mughirah bin Uthman told me, he said: I heard Anas bin Malik say: I have vowed to the Most Merciful to fast. He said: Silence. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, he said: By fasting he means silence. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, he said: I heard Anas recite: I have vowed to the Most Merciful to fast and remain silent. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast. As for his saying a fast, it means that I fasted from food, drink, and speech. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, that there were those among the Children of Israel who, when they exerted themselves, would fast from speech as they fasted from food, except for the remembrance of God. So he said that to her, and she said: I fast from speech as I fast from food, except for the remembrance of God. So when they spoke to her, she pointed to him, and they said, How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child? So he answered them and said, “Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Scripture,” until he reached, That is Jesus, the son of Mary, the word of truth about which they are in doubt. They differed about the reason for which he ordered her to fast from human speech. Some of them said: He ordered her to do that because she did not have an apparent argument before the people, and that was because she came while she was widowed and had a child, to refrain from speaking so that it would suffice her, so she ordered her child to speak. Who said that? Harun bin Ishaq Al-Hamadani narrated to us, saying: Mus`ab bin Al-Muqaddam narrated to us, saying: Israel narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Haritha, who said: I was with Ibn Mas`ud when two men came, one of them greeted him and the other did not. He said: What is the matter with you? His companions said: He swore that he would not speak to the people today. Abdullah said: Speak to the people and greet them, for that is a woman who knows that no one will believe her that she became pregnant without a husband, meaning Mary, peace be upon her. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, when Jesus said to Mary, Do not grieve, she said: How can I not grieve when you are with me, neither a husband nor a slave? What excuse do I have before the people? I wish I had died before this and was in oblivion, forgotten. Jesus said to her: I will suffice you in speaking. But if you see anyone among mankind, say, ‘Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, so I will not speak to any human being today.’ He said: All of this was Jesus’ speech to his mother. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih: If you see anyone among mankind, say, ‘Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful to fast, so I will not speak to any human being today.’ Then I will suffice you in speaking. Others said: This was a sign for Mary and her son. Who said that? Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, he said in some of the letters: silence, and that is because you will not find an ignorant woman saying: I vowed as Mary vowed, not to speak one day until night, and God only made that a sign for Mary and her son, and it is not permissible for anyone to vow silence one day until night. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, so he recited: Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast. And it was read in the first letter: silence, and it was only a sign that God sent to Mary and her son. Others said: Rather, she was fasting on that day, and the fasting person at that time was fasting from food, drink, and speaking to people, so Mary was permitted to speak for the amount of time that day while she was fasting. Who said that? Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: If you see anyone among mankind speaking to you, say, ‘Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, so I will not speak to any human being today.’ So whoever fasted at that time would not speak until evening. So it was said to her: Do not say more than this.
19:27: God Almighty says: When Jesus said that to his mother, she felt reassured, submitted to God’s command, and carried him until she brought him to her people. Ibn Hamid also told us: Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: He made her, meaning Mary, forget the distress of the affliction and the fear of the people because of what she had heard from the angels about the good report of Jesus, until he spoke to her, meaning Jesus, and the fulfillment of what God had promised her came to her, she bore it and then returned with it to her people. Al-Saddī said about this: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: When she gave birth to him, Satan went and informed the Children of Israel that Mary had given birth, so they came rushing forward, so they called her, and she brought him to her people, carrying him. And His saying, They said, ‘O Mary, you have certainly done a thing unprecedented.’ God Almighty says: So when they saw Mary, and saw with her the child she had given birth to, they said to her: O Mary, you have done a wondrous thing, and you have brought about a great event, and every doer of a work that he has done well and perfected has done it wonderfully, as the rajaz poet said: You fed me a stone date with which you used to scatter the fleas. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, Fara’a, he said: Great. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, You have certainly done something unprecedented, he said: great. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, You have certainly done something unprecedented. He said: Great. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When they saw her and saw him with her, they said: O Mary, You have certainly done a thing outrageous: meaning, the immorality that is not close.
19:28: The people of interpretation differed about the reason for which she was called: O sister of Aaron, and who was this Aaron whom God mentioned, and he informed that they attributed Mary to her as his sister, so some of them said: She was called O sister of Aaron as an attribution from them to righteousness, because the righteous people among them were called Aaron, and not Aaron, the brother of Moses. Who said that? Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, O sister of Aaron, he said: There was a righteous man among the Children of Israel called Aaron, so they likened her to him, and they said: O you who resemble Aaron in righteousness. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, O sister of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste. He said: She was from a family known for their righteousness, and not for their corruption. Some people are known for their righteousness and have children through it, and others are known for their corruption and have children through it. Aaron was a reformer who was beloved by his clan. He was not Aaron, the brother of Moses, but another Aaron. He said: It was mentioned to us that forty thousand people accompanied his funeral procession on the day he died, all of them named Aaron from the Children of Israel. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Abi Sidqah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, he said: I was informed that Ka`b said: His saying, O sister of Aaron, does not refer to Aaron, the brother of Moses. He said: Aisha said to him: You have lied. He said: O Mother of the Believers, if the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said it, then he is more knowledgeable and informed, otherwise I find that there are six hundred years between them. He said: So she was silent. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, O sister of Aaron, he said: A name that matches a name, how many nations are there between Aaron and them, many nations. Abu Kurayb, Ibn Al-Muthanna, Sufyan, Ibn Wakee’ and Abu Al-Sa’ib narrated: Abdullah Ibn Idris Al-Awdi narrated: I heard my father mention on the authority of Samak Ibn Harb, on the authority of Alqamah Ibn Wa’il, on the authority of Al-Mughirah Ibn Shu’bah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me to the people of Najran, and they said to me: Do you not recite O sister of Aaron? I said: Yes, and you know what happened between Jesus and Moses. So I returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. He said: Why did you not tell them that they used to water their children through their prophets and the righteous before them? Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us: Amr told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Alqamah bin Wa’il, on the authority of Al-Mughirah bin Shu’bah, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me to the people of Najran on some of his errands. They said: Didn’t your Prophet claim that Aaron, the brother of Mary, was the brother of Moses? I did not know what to say to them until I returned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him. He said: They used to name people after the names of those who came before them. Some of them said: He meant Aaron, the brother of Moses, and Mary was attributed to him as his sister because she was from his descendants. It is said to the Tamimi: O brother of Tamim, and to the Mudarite: O brother of Mudar. Who said that? Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: O sister of Aaron. He said: She was from the sons of Aaron, the brother of Moses, and it is as you say: O brother of the sons of so-and-so. Others said: Rather, he was one of their men who was a wicked man who was openly wicked, so they attributed it to him. Abu Jaafar said: The correct statement about this is what was reported from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which we mentioned, and that she was attributed to a man from her people. His saying, Your father was not a bad man, means: Your father was not a bad man who committed indecencies. And your mother was not a prostitute, means: Your mother was not a fornicator. As Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, And your mother was not a prostitute, he said: an adulteress. And he said: And your mother was not a prostitute, and he did not say: a prostitute, because that is something that describes women and not men, so it is treated like a menstruating or divorced woman. Some of them likened that to their saying: a new cloak and a murdered woman.
19:29: God Almighty says: When her people said that to her, she told them what Jesus had ordered her to say to them, then she motioned to Jesus to speak to him. As Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: When they said to her, Your father was not a bad man, nor was your mother unchaste, she told them what God had commanded her to do. Then when they wanted her to speak after that, she pointed to it, to Jesus. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, So she pointed to him, he said: She ordered them to speak to him. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih: She pointed to him. He said: She pointed to him to speak to him. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his saying so she pointed to him is that they spoke to him. And His statement, They said, ‘How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?’ God Almighty says, Her people said to her: How can we speak to one who is in the cradle? And in His statement, who is in the cradle, a child, there is a meaning of completion, not that which requires report, and that is similar in meaning to the word was in His statement, Was I anything but a human messenger? (al-Isra’ 17:93). Rather, the meaning of that is: Am I anything but a human messenger? And was I found or sent? And as Zuhair ibn Abi Salma said: A free woman, Arhabiya, rebuked him, and the color of the night was like apricot. Meaning: It has become or has been found. It was said that what is meant by the cradle in this place is: his mother’s lap. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Whoever is in the cradle as a child. The cradle is the stone. Abu Jaafar said: We have explained the meaning of the cradle in the past with its evidence, so there is no need to repeat it in this place.
19:30: God Almighty says: When Mary's people said to her, How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child? and they thought that this was a mockery of them, Jesus said to them, speaking on behalf of his mother, "Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Scripture." And when she pointed to Jesus in what was mentioned about them, they became angry. As Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: When she pointed to Jesus to them, they became angry and said: Her mockery of us when she ordered us to speak to this boy is more severe for us than her adultery. They said: How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child? Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih: They said, ‘How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?’ So Jesus answered them about it and said to them, “Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.”... the verse. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, They said, ‘How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?’ He said to them, “Indeed, I am a servant of God. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.” So he recited until he reached, And has not made me a wretched tyrant. They said, Indeed, this is a great matter. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: “How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child? He said: I am the servant of God.” Jesus did not speak until that time, when “They said: How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?” And his saying: He has given me the Book, means that the speaker says: Or He gave him the Book and the revelation before he was created in his mother’s womb, for the meaning of that is contrary to what is thought, rather its meaning is: And He decreed on the day He decreed the affairs of His creation until He gave me the Book. As Bishr bin Adam told me, he said: Ad-Dahhak told us, meaning Ibn Mukhallad, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: He gave me the Book, meaning: He decreed that the Book would be given to me in the past. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abu Asim told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, “Indeed, I am a servant of God. He has given me the Book,” he said: the judgment. Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding God’s statement, “Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Scripture.” He said: He decreed that the Scripture should be given to me. And his saying, And He made me a prophet. I have explained the meaning of prophet and the differences of opinion among those who differ about it, and the correct statement about it according to us with its evidence in what has passed, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it. Mujahid used to say about the meaning of the Prophet alone what: Muhammad bin Amr told us: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The Prophet alone is the one who speaks and to whom revelation is sent, and he is not sent.
19:31: And his saying, And made me blessed, the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: Its meaning is: And made me beneficial. Who said that? Sulayman bin Abd al-Rahman bin Hammad al-Talhi told me: Al-Ala’ told us, on the authority of Aisha, the wife of Layth, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: And He made me blessed, he said: beneficial. Others said: His blessing was enjoining good and forbidding evil. Who said that? Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Khunais al-Makhzumi told us: I heard Wahib ibn al-Ward, a client of Banu Makhzum, say: A scholar met another scholar who was above him in knowledge, and said to him: May God have mercy on you, what of my knowledge have you made public? He said: Enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, for it is the religion of God with which He sent His prophets to His servants. The jurists have agreed upon the statement of God: And has made me blessed wherever I may be. It was said: What is its blessing? He said: Enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong wherever it may be. Others said: The meaning of this is: He made me a teacher of goodness. Who said that? Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me: Sufyan told us regarding his statement, And He has made me blessed wherever I may be, he said: A teacher of goodness. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And He has made me blessed wherever I may be, he said: A teacher of goodness wherever I may be. And his saying, And He enjoined upon me prayer and zakat, means: And He decreed that He enjoined upon me prayer and zakat, meaning preserving the limits of prayer and performing it as He enjoined upon me. And zakat has two meanings: One of them is: The zakat of wealth, which is to be paid. And the other is: Purifying the body from the filth of sins, so its meaning is: And He enjoined upon me to abandon sins and avoid transgressions. His saying, As long as I am alive, means: As long as I was alive in this world and existing. This shows that the meaning of zakat in this context is: purifying the body from sins, because what Jesus, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, is described as is that he did not save anything for tomorrow, so zakat on money is obligatory upon him, unless the zakat that was imposed upon him was charity on everything that was in excess of his strength, in which case that would be a correct interpretation.
19:32: God Almighty says, informing about what Jesus said to the al-Nas 114:And He made me blessed and dutiful: meaning He made me dutiful to my mother. And dutifulness is being dutiful, it is said: He is dutiful to his father, and dutiful to him, and the readers of the regions read this letter with the opening of the ba. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Nahik that: Ibn Humayd narrated: Yahya ibn Wadeh narrated: Abdul-Mu'min narrated: Abu Nahik read, And be dutiful to my mother from the words of Jesus, peace be upon him. Abu Nahik said: He enjoined upon me prayer, zakat, and being dutiful to my parents, just as he enjoined upon me that. So Abu Nahik interpreted the words to mean, And be dutiful to my mother as being from the report of Jesus, from God's enjoining upon him that, just as his words, And enjoined upon me prayer and zakat are from his report of God's enjoining upon him that. So according to this opinion, the accusative of birr must mean the implementation of the enjoining in it, because prayer and zakat, even though they are in the genitive case in the wording, are in the accusative case because they are the objects of them. And His saying, And He did not make me a wretched tyrant, means: And He did not make me arrogant towards God in what He commanded me to do and what He forbade me from doing. And wretched, but He humbled me to obey Him and made me humble. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: It was mentioned to us that he - meaning Jesus - used to say: Ask me, for my heart is soft, and I am small in my soul, because of the humility God gave him. And Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And dutiful to my mother and did not make me a wretched tyrant. It was mentioned to us that a woman saw the son of Mary bringing the dead back to life, and healing the blind and the leper, in signs that God had given him authority over and permitted him to do. So she said: Blessed is the womb that bore you, and the breast that nursed you. So the Prophet of God, the son of Mary, said in response to her: Blessed is he who recites the Book of God and follows what is in it, And did not make me a wretched tyrant. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Hussein narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Katheer narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Waqid Abu Raja, on the authority of some of the people of knowledge, he said: You will not find a disobedient person except that you will find him a tyrant and a wretched person. Then he recited: And dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a wretched tyrant. He said: And you will not find a person of bad character except that you will find him arrogant and proud. Then he recited: “And those whom your right hands possess. Indeed, God does not like anyone who is arrogant and boastful.” (An-Nisa’: 36)
19:33: And his saying, "And peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised alive," means: And security from God upon me from Satan and his soldiers on the day I was born, lest they should harm me as they harm those who are born at birth, by stabbing them, and on the day I die, from the terror of the rising, and on the day I am raised alive on the Day of Resurrection, lest I be struck by the terror that befalls people when they witness the terrors of that day. Ibn Hamid also told us, saying: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, “And peace be upon me the day I was born and the day I die and the day I am raised alive.” He said: He tells them in the story of his report about himself, that he has no father and that he will die and then be raised alive. God Almighty says, That is Jesus, the son of Mary - the word of truth about which they are in dispute.
19:34: God Almighty says: This one whose description I have explained to you and whose report I have informed you of, regarding the matter of the boy whom Mary carried, is Jesus, son of Mary, and this description is his description, and this report is his report, and it is the word of truth, meaning that this report that I have related to you is the word of truth, and the speech that I have recited to you is the word of God and His report, not report other than it, in which there is confusion and doubt, addition and subtraction, according to what God Almighty used to say: So say about Jesus, O people, this statement that God has informed you about him, not what the Jews said, who claimed that he was not of sound mind and that he was a lying magician, nor what the Christians said, that he had a son for God, and that God did not take a son, and that is not appropriate for Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, That is Jesus, the son of Mary, the word of truth, he said: God is the Truth. Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: They used to say about this letter in the recitation of Abdullah: He said the truth about which they are in doubt. He said: The word of God. If the interpretation of this is directed to: That is Jesus, son of Mary, the true word, meaning that is the true word, then the definite article is deleted from the word and added to the truth, as it was said: Indeed, this is the certain truth (al-Waqi’ah 56:95). And as it was said: The promise of truth which they were promised (al-Ahqaf 46:16), it would be a correct interpretation. The reciters differed in their reading of this. The reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as the saying of truth, with the saying raised, according to the meaning I described, and they made it in its parsing dependent on Jesus, like an adjective for him. The matter in its parsing, in my opinion, is not as said by those who claimed that it is raised as an adjective for Jesus, unless the meaning of the saying is the word, according to what we mentioned about Ibrahim, from his interpretation of that in this way, then it is correct for it to be an adjective for Jesus. Otherwise, in my opinion, it is raised by an implied word, which is this saying of truth, as a beginning. This is because the report had ended about the story of Jesus and his mother when he said, That is Jesus, son of Mary, then the report began with the truth in what the nations doubt about the matter of Jesus, is this saying, which God informed His servants about him, and no other. Asim bin Abi al-Najud and Abdullah bin Amir read it in the accusative case, as if they intended by that the source: That is Jesus, son of Mary, a true saying, then the definite article was inserted into it. As for what was mentioned by Ibn Masoud regarding his reading that Jesus, son of Mary, said the truth, it means saying the truth, like play and shame, and blame and blame. Abu Ja`far said: The correct reading of this in our view is to raise it, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it. As for the statement of God Almighty, about which they are in doubt, it means: about which they dispute and differ, from their saying: I disputed with so-and-so, if you argued with him and disputed with him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, That is Jesus, the son of Mary, the word of truth about which they are in dispute, the Jews and Christians were in dispute about him. As for the Jews, they claimed that he was a lying magician, and as for the Christians, they claimed that he was the son of God, the third of three, and a god, and they all lied, but he is the servant of God and His Messenger, and His Word and His Spirit. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement, about which they are in doubt, he said: They differed, and a group said: He is the servant and prophet of God, so they believed in him. A group said: Rather, he is God. A group said: He is the son of God. Blessed and exalted be He above what they say, far above. He said: That is what he said: Then the parties differed among themselves (Maryam 19:37) and what is in Az-Zukhruf. Decius, Nestorius, and Mar Ya’qub said: When God raised Jesus, one of them said: He is God, and the other said: The Son of God, and the other said: The Word of God and His servant. So the two slanderers said: My saying is more similar to your saying, and your saying is more similar to my saying than this one’s saying, so come, let us fight them. So they fought them and Israel subdued them. So they brought out four men from among them, each group brought out their scholar. So they doubted Jesus when he was raised. So one of them said: He is God, He descended to the earth and gave life to whomever He gave life, and caused death to whomever He caused to die, then He ascended to the heavens. They are the Jacobites. So the three said: You have lied. Then two of them said to the third: You say about him. He said: He is the Son of God. They are the Nestorians. So the two said: You have lied. Then one of the two said to the other: Say about him. He said: He is the third of three: God is God, and he is God, and his mother is God. They are the Israelites, the kings of the Christians. The fourth said: You have lied. He is the servant of God, His Messenger, and His spirit. And his word, and they are the Muslims, so each man of them had followers for what he said, so they fought, and he prevailed over the Muslims, and that is the saying of God And they kill those who enjoin justice among the people (Al Imran 3:21). Qatada said: They are the ones about whom God said So the parties differed (Maryam 19:37), they differed about it and became parties.
19:35: God Almighty says: Those who said: Jesus is the son of God have certainly disbelieved, and they have greatly slandered him. It is not appropriate for God to take a son, and that is not appropriate for Him and will not happen. Rather, He created everything below Him. This is similar to the statement of Amr ibn Ahmar: In the head of a nobleman from a lofty phoenix, no plain or mountain can be sought beyond it. And from His saying that He should take in the nominative case with was. And His saying Glory be to Him He says: To glorify God and to acquit Him from having what the disbelievers who say: Jesus is the son of God have added to Him. And His saying When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, “Be, and it is. The Most High says: God only began the creation of Jesus in the beginning, and brought him into being, without a stallion, so that his mother would be fertile. But He said to him, Be, and he was, because that is how He creates and invents things. He only says when He decrees the creation of something or its bringing it into being: Be, and it is existing and new. His creation is not too great for Him, because He does not create it with difficulty and effort, nor does He bring it into being with treatment and hardship.
19:36: And his saying, And indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. The reciters differed in reading that. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as and God is my Lord and your Lord. The Arabists differed in the reason for opening the an when it is opened. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: It is opened in response to Isa and in apposition to it, meaning: That is Isa, son of Mary, and that is because God is my Lord and your Lord. If that is the case, then an is a nominative, and it can be interpreted as a genitive, as he said, That is because your Lord would not destroy the cities unjustly. (Al-An'am: 131) He said: If you opened it on his saying And He enjoined upon me that it is God, it would be a reason. Some of the Basrans said: And this was also mentioned from Abu Amr ibn al-Ala, and he was one of those who read it with the opening. Rather, an is opened with the interpretation and He decreed that God is my Lord and your Lord. The majority of the Kufi readers read it as And God with a kasra on in meaning sequence, as in the saying He only says to him. It was mentioned on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b that he used to read it as He only says to him, ‘Be,’ and it is. Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord,” without a waw. Abu Ja`far said: The reading that we prefer in this regard is the kasra as a beginning. If it is read in this way, it has no place. It may be permissible for it to be in apposition to in which is with his statement, “He said, ‘Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Book’” and Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord. If someone, among those who read it in the accusative case, were to say: It is in apposition to the Book, meaning: He gave me the Book, and He gave me that God is my Lord and your Lord, that would be a good interpretation. The meaning of the statement is: And I and you, O people, are all servants of God, so worship Him alone and no one else. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: He made a covenant with them when he informed them about himself, his birth, his death, and his mission, that “God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.” That is, I and you are the servants of God, so worship Him and do not worship anyone other than Him. And his saying, This is a straight path, means: This that I have recommended to you and informed you that God has commanded me to do is the straight path, which whoever follows it will be saved and whoever follows it will be guided, because it is the religion of God that He commanded His prophets to do.
19:37: God Almighty says: So the disputants differed about Jesus, and they became divided parties from among his people. As Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told me, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, Then the parties differed among themselves, he said: The People of the Book. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Then the parties differed among themselves, it was mentioned to us that when the son of Mary was raised, the Children of Israel chose four of their jurists, and they said to the first: What do you say about Jesus? He said: He is God who descended to earth, created what He created, and gave life to what He gave life, then ascended to heaven. Some people followed him in that, and the Jacobites were among the Christians, and the other three said: We bear witness that you are a liar. They said to the second: What do you say about Jesus? He said: He is the son of God. Some people followed him in that, and the Nestorians were among the Christians, and the other two said: We bear witness that you are a liar. They said to the third: What do you say about Jesus? He said: He is a god, and his mother is a god, and God is a god. Some people followed him in that, and the Israelite was from the Christians. The fourth said: I bear witness that you are a liar, but he is the servant and messenger of God, he is the word of God and His spirit. So the people argued, and the Muslim said: I ask you by God, do you know that Jesus used to feed people, and that God, the Blessed and Exalted, does not feed people? They said: By God, yes. He said: Do you know that Jesus used to sleep? They said: By God, yes. He said: So the Muslim argued with them. He said: So the people fought. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Jacobites appeared on that day and the Muslims were afflicted, so God revealed in that Quran: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of God and kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice among the people - give them tidings of a painful punishment. (Al Imran 3:21) Al-Hasan told us, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: Then the parties differed among themselves. They differed about it and became parties. And His saying, So woe to those who disbelieve from the sight of a tremendous Day, means: So woe to those who disbelieve in God, from those who claim that Jesus was born of God, and other disbelievers in Him from witnessing a tremendous Day, which is the Day of Resurrection. Qatada used to say in his interpretation of this: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, God said: So woe to those who disbelieve from the scene of a tremendous Day. They witnessed a tremendous terror.
19:38: God Almighty says, informing about the state of those who disbelieve in Him, who make rivals for Him, and who claim that He has a son on the day they come to Him in the Hereafter: If they were blind in this world to seeing the truth, and to looking at the proofs of God that indicate His Oneness, and deaf to hearing the verses of His Book, and what God’s messengers called them to in it of acknowledging His Oneness, and what He sent His prophets with, then what will they hear on the day they come to their Lord in the Hereafter, and what will they see on that day when sight and hearing will not benefit them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, I hear and see them, that, by God, is on the Day of Resurrection. They heard when hearing did not benefit them, and they saw when sight did not benefit them. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, I hear them and see them, he said: I hear a people and I see them. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said: I will hear about them and see them on the Day they come to us on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah, he said: I hear their talk today and I see how they will be treated on the day they come to Us. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd, regarding His statement, I will hear about them and see the Day they come to Us, he said: This is the Day of Resurrection, but as for this world, no. There was a veil over their eyes, and in their ears was a deafness in this world. Then when the Day of Resurrection came, they saw and heard, but they did not benefit. And he recited, “Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us [to the world]; we will do righteousness. Indeed, we are [now] certain.” (al-Sajdah 32:12) And His statement, But the wrongdoers today are in manifest error, God Almighty says: But the disbelievers who attributed to Him what is not of His description, and fabricated lies about Him today in this world, are in manifest error. He says: In straying from the path of truth, and taking a non-straight path, clearly deviating from the path of guidance and right direction, for whoever contemplates it and thinks about it, and is guided to the right path.
19:39: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And warn, O Muhammad, these polytheists of the Day of their regret and remorse, for what they neglected in the side of God, and their dwellings in Paradise will be inherited by the people of faith in God and obedience to Him, and they will enter the dwellings of the people of faith in God from the Fire, and both groups will be certain of eternal life, and the life after which there is no death, so what regret and remorse. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhail, who said: Abu al-Zura’ told us, on the authority of Abdullah, in a story he mentioned, who said: There is no soul but that it looks at a house in Paradise and a house in Hell, and it is the Day of Regret. The people of Hell will see the house that God had prepared for them if they had believed, and it will be said to them: If you had believed and done righteous deeds, this that you see in Paradise would have been yours, so regret will overtake them, and the people of Paradise will see the house that is in Hell, and it will be said: If God had not been gracious to you. Abu al-Sa’ib narrated: Mu’awiyah narrated to us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and will be made to stand between Paradise and Hell like a white ram. It will be said: O people of Paradise, do you recognize this?’ They will look up and say: ‘Yes, this is death.’ It will be said: O people of Hell, do you recognize this?’ They will look up and say: ‘Yes, this is death.’ Then it will be ordered to be slaughtered. It will be said: O people of Paradise, eternal life and no death. O people of Hell, eternal life and no death.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘And warn them of the Day of Regret when the matter is decided while they are in heedlessness and they do not believe.’ And he pointed with his hand to the world.” Ubayd ibn Asbat ibn Muhammad told me: My father told me, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding this verse: ‘And warn them of the Day of Regret,’ he said: ‘O people of Paradise, it will be called out, and they will stretch out their heads and look. Then it will be called out, ‘O people of the Fire,’ and they will stretch out their heads and look. Then it will be said: ‘Do you know death?’ He said: ‘And they will say: ‘No.’ He said: ‘Then death will be brought in the form of a white ram, and it will be said: ‘This is death.’ Then it will be taken and slaughtered. He said: ‘Then it will be called out, ‘O people of the Fire, eternity and no death.’ O people of Paradise, eternity and no death.’ He said: Then he recited: ‘And warn them of the Day of Regret when the matter has been decided.’” Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, saying: Ibn Abbas said, regarding His statement, And warn them of the Day of Regret, he said: God will depict death in the form of a white ram, which will be slaughtered. He said: The people of Hell will despair of death, and will not hope for it, and regret will overtake them because of their eternal stay in Hell. In it also is the greatest terror, and the people of Paradise will be safe from death, and will not fear it. They will be safe from death, which is the greatest terror, because they will remain eternal in Paradise. Ibn Jurayj said: The people of Hell will be gathered when death is slaughtered and the two groups will watch, so that is His statement, When the matter is decided, he said: Death is slaughtered, while they are in heedlessness. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of his father, that he told him that he heard Ubayd ibn Umair say in his al-Qasas 28:Death is brought as if it were a beast, and it is slaughtered while the people watch. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And warn them of the Day of Regret, he said: The Day of Resurrection, and he recited, That a soul may say, ‘Oh, how I regret what I neglected in my duty to God!’ (al-Zumar 39:56). Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And warn them of the Day of Regret is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. God has made it great and warned His servants about it. His statement, When the matter is decided means: When He has finished ruling for the people of Hell to remain there forever, and for the people of Paradise to remain there forever, by slaughtering death. His statement, And they are in heedlessness means: And these polytheists are in heedlessness of what God will do to them on the Day when they come to Him, emerging from their graves, by His immortality in Hell, and His inheriting their dwellings in Paradise to others. And they do not believe God, the Exalted, says: And they do not believe in the Resurrection and the Resurrection, and God’s recompense to them for their evil deeds, with what He has informed us that He will recompense them with.
19:40: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not be saddened by the denial of these polytheists towards you, O Muhammad, regarding the truth that you have brought them, for to Us is their return and their destiny and the destiny of all creation except them, and We are the inheritors of the earth and all the people on it, through their annihilation from it, and its remaining without any owner other than Us, then upon Us is the reward of every worker among them for his work, when he returns to Us, the good among them for his good, and the evildoer for his evil.
19:41: God Almighty says to His Prophet: And mention, O Muhammad, in the Book of God, Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful. So tell these polytheists his stories and the stories of his father. He was a truthful man. He says: He was one of the people of truthfulness in his speech, report, and promises. He did not lie. The truthful man is the active participle of truthfulness. We have already explained this, so there is no need to repeat it here. A prophet means: God had informed him and revealed to him.
19:42: And His saying, When he said to his father, he says: Remember when he said to his father, O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear? He says: What do you do by worshipping an idol that does not hear, nor see anything, nor avail you at all? He says: Nor ward off any harm from you, it is only a pictured image that neither harms nor benefits. He says: What do you do by worshipping something that has this description? Worship the One who, when you call upon Him, hears your call, and when you are surrounded, sees you and supports you, and when harm befalls you, He wards it off. The Arabists differed about the reason for the inclusion of the letter ha’ in the word ya abat O father. Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: If you stop on it, you say: ya abah O father, and it is a ha’ that was added, like when you say: ya ummah O mother, then you say: ya umm O mother if you connect it. However, since the word father has two letters, it was as if he had omitted it, so the ha’ became necessary, and the ya’ became as if it came after it. That is why they said: ya aba aqbal O father, come, and the ta’ was made for femininity. It is permissible to shorten the word from ya aba aqbal, because it is permissible to call what you add to yourself in meaning with a damma, like the Arabs say: ya rab ighfir li O Lord, forgive me, and you stop in the Qur’an: ya aba fi al-kitab O father, in the book. Some Arabs may stop on the ha’ with the ta’. Some grammarians of Kufa said: The ha’ with ‘aba’ and ‘ummah is a ha’ of pause. It became so common in their speech that it became like the ha’ of femininity. They introduced the addition to it. Whoever asks for the addition, it is with the ta’ and nothing else, because you ask for the ya’ after it, and the ha’ then is only a ta’, like when you say: ya abat, and nothing else. Whoever says: ya abah, he is the one who stops with the ha’, because he does not ask for the ya’ after it. Whoever says: ya abat, he stops with the ta’, and it is permissible with the ha’. As for the ta’, it is because of the request for the alif of lamentation, so the ha’ became a ta’ for that reason. Stopping with the ha’ is far-fetched, except for whoever says: ya Umaimah, making this fathah from the fathah of tarkhīm, as if this is the end of the noun. He said: This is far-fetched.
19:43: God Almighty says: Abraham said to his father: O my father, God has given me knowledge that He has not given you, so follow me. He says: So accept my advice. I will guide you to a straight path. He says: I will show you the guidance of the straight path in which you will not go astray if you adhere to it, and it is the religion of God in which there is no crookedness.
19:44: God Almighty says: O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed Satan has been disobedient to God. The disobedient is the one who disobeys, just as the knowledgeable is the one who has knowledge. Some Arabs have said: The disobedient is the one who disobeys, the knowledgeable is the one who knows, and they have cited as evidence for their statement the words of Tarif bin Tamim al-Anbari: Or whenever a tribe came to Ukaz, they would send to their chief to look for They said: Their chief said, meaning: their most knowledgeable person, and God knows best.
19:45: He says: O my father, I know that if you die worshipping Satan, he will afflict you with a punishment from the punishment of God. Then you will be a friend of Satan. He says: You will be a friend to him instead of God, and God will disown you, and you will perish. Fear in this context means knowledge, just as awe means knowledge, in His statement: So we feared that he would overburden them through transgression and disbelief. (al-Kahf 18:80)
19:46: God Almighty says: Abraham's father said to Abraham, when Abraham called him to worship God and abandon the worship of Satan, and to disavow idols and statues: Do you want to worship my gods, O Abraham? If you do not stop mentioning them badly, I will stone you. He says: I will stone you with words, and that is cursing and ugly speech. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: Do you reject my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will stone you with insults and words. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said, regarding his statement, If you do not desist, I will stone you, he said: By word, I will curse you. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding his statement, I will stone you, meaning: I will stone the statement. As for his saying, And leave me alone for a long time, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: And leave me alone for a long time and an age. And they directed the meaning of al-mulla to the term al-mulla of time, which is the long term of it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Abu Dawud told us: Muhammad bin Abi al-Waddah told us, on the authority of Abd al-Karim, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And leave me alone for a long time, he said: for an age. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement for a while he said: for a while. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And leave me alone for a long time. He said for a long time. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement: And leave me alone for a long time, he said: A long time. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: And leave me alone for a long time. He said: for an age. And age means a long time. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr: And leave me alone for a long time. He said: For a long time. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And leave me alone for a long time, he said: Forever. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Leave me alone, safe from my punishment of you. They attributed the meaning of full to the people’s saying: So-and-so is full of this matter, meaning that he is well-versed in it and rich in it. It is as if the meaning of the statement was, for them,: Leave me alone, and your honor is safe from my punishment, and your body is free from my harm. Who said that? Ali bin Dawud told me, he said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And avoid me completely, meaning: avoid me completely. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And avoid me for a long time, he said: Avoid me safely before a punishment befalls you from me. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And leave me alone for a long time, he said: Safely. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya bin Katheer bin Dirham Abu Ghassan told us: Qara bin Khalid told us, on the authority of Atiyah al-Jadali: And leave me alone for a long time. He said: Safely. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And avoid me for a long time: Avoid me in peace, so that no reproach will befall you because of me. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two opinions regarding the interpretation of the verse, in my opinion, is the opinion of the one who said: Its meaning is: And leave me alone, safe from my punishment, because it follows His saying: If you do not desist, I will stone you. This is a threat from Him to him if he does not desist from mentioning his gods in a bad way, that He will stone him with a bad word, and what is more appropriate to follow that is to come forward to Him by desisting from it before the punishment befalls him. As for the command to leave him for a long time, there is no basis for it.
19:47: God the Almighty says: Abraham said to his father when he threatened him with evil words and punishment for his advice to him and his calling to God: Peace be upon you, my father. He says: It is a security from me to you that I will not return to what you hate, and for calling to me what you threatened me with punishment for, but I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord meaning: But I will ask my Lord to cover your sins by pardoning you from punishing you for them. He has been gracious to me meaning: I have known my Lord to be gracious to me, answering my call when I call upon Him. It is said from him: So-and-so was gracious to me. I have explained that with its evidence previously, so there is no need to repeat it here. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, He was kind to me, meaning: gentle. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, Indeed, He was kind to me, he said: Indeed, He was gentle with me, for kind means gentle.
19:48: And His statement: And I will withdraw from you and what you call upon besides God means: And I will avoid you and what you call upon besides God of idols and statues And I will call upon my Lord means: And I will call upon my Lord, with sincere worship of Him and singling Him out as Lord Perhaps I will not be wretched in calling upon my Lord means: Perhaps I will not be wretched in calling upon my Lord, but He will answer my call and give me what I ask of Him.
19:49: God Almighty says: So when Abraham had withdrawn from his people and from the worship of what they used to worship besides God of idols, We relieved his loneliness from being separated from them, and We replaced him with someone better than them and more honored by God than them, so We gave him his son Isaac, and his grandson Jacob, son of Isaac. And each of them We made a prophet. He says: And We made them all, meaning by all Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, prophets. God Almighty said: And each of them We made a prophet. So He made it singular, and did not say prophets, to make the word each singular.
19:50: And We bestowed upon them of Our mercy. God Almighty says: And We provided for all of them, meaning Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, of Our mercy. And what He bestowed upon them of His mercy was what He expanded for them in this immediate world of His abundant provision, and He enriched them with His grace. And His statement: And We made for them a high reputation for truthfulness. God Almighty says: And We granted them good praise and beautiful mention from the people. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: And We made for them a tongue of truth, high, meaning: good praise. And the Most High described the tongue that was made for them as high, because all people of religions praise them well, and the Arabs say: The tongue of so-and-so has come to me, meaning his praise or his blame? And from this is the statement of Amer bin Al-Harith: I have been given a tongue that I do not delight in, from its loftiness, neither astonishment nor mockery. It is narrated: There is no lying or mockery in it. She came as a translator, I would have been wary of her if pity and caution had been of any use to me. Translated: It is thought of.
19:51: God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And mention, O Muhammad, in Our Book which We revealed to you, Moses, son of Imran, and tell your people that he was sincere. The readers differed in their reading of this. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians read it as inna kan khulus with a kasra on the lam of mukhlis, meaning: he was sincere in his worship to God, and singled Him out in divinity, without making any partner for Him in it. The majority of the readers of Kufa, except for Asim, read it as inna kan khulus with a fatha on the lam of mukhlis, meaning: God had sincerely chosen Moses for His message, and made him a prophet and messenger. Abu Jaafar said: The correct statement in this regard, in my opinion, is that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sincere in his worship of God, sincere in his message and prophethood, so whichever of them the reader recites, he is correct. And he was a messenger means: And God was a messenger to his people, the Children of Israel, and the one to whom He sent him was a prophet.
