19:52: God Almighty says: And We called to Moses from the side of the mountain, meaning by the right, the right of Moses, because the mountain has no right or left, but rather it is as it is said: He stood to the right of the qiblah and to the left of it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: From the right side of the Mount, he said: The right side of the mountain. We have explained the meaning of the Mount and the differences of opinion among those who differed about it, and we have indicated the correct statement in what has passed, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. And His statement: And We brought him near, in private conversation, the Most High says: And We brought him near, in private conversation, just as one says: So-and-so is the companion of so-and-so and his drinking companion, or the friend of so-and-so and his companions. And He mentioned that God, the Most High, brought him near, until he heard the scratching of the pen. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Yahya told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We brought him near for a private conversation. He said: He brought him near until he heard the scratching of the pen. Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Tusi told us: Yahya ibn Abi Bakr told us: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, who said: I think it was on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And We brought him near for a private conversation, he said: Between the fourth heaven, or he said: the seventh, and the Throne there are seventy thousand veils: a veil of light, a veil of darkness, a veil of light, and a veil of darkness. So he kept bringing Moses near until there was a veil between him and Him, and he heard the scratching of the pen. “He said: My Lord, show me, that I may look at You.” (al-A’raf 7:143) Ali bin Sahl told us: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, who said: He brought him close to him until he heard the scratching of the pen. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Maysarah: And We brought him near for a private conversation. He said: He brought him near until he heard the scratching of the pen on the tablet. Shu’bah said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, accompanied him. Qatada said about this: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And We brought him near for a private conversation, he said: He was saved by his truthfulness.
19:53: And His statement: And We bestowed upon him, out of Our mercy, his brother Aaron, meaning: And We bestowed upon Moses, out of Our mercy, his brother Aaron, a prophet, meaning: We supported him with his prophethood and aided him with it. As Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Ibn Abbas said, regarding his statement, And We bestowed upon him, out of Our mercy, his brother Aaron, a prophet, he said: Aaron was older than Moses, but he meant that He bestowed upon him his prophethood.
19:54: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And mention, O Muhammad, in this Book, Ishmael, son of Abraham, and relate his story. Indeed, he did not lie about his promise, nor did he break it. But when he promised his Lord, or one of His servants, a promise, he fulfilled it. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement: He was true to his promise, he said: He did not make a promise to his Lord without fulfilling it. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Amr ibn al-Harith told me that Sahl ibn Aqil told him that Ismail, peace be upon him, promised a man a place to come to, but he came and the man forgot. Ismail stayed with him and spent the night until the man came the next day. He said: Have you not left here? He said: No. He said: I forgot. He said: I would not leave until you came. So he was truthful in that.
19:55: God Almighty says: And he used to enjoin his family to establish prayer and to give “zakat, and his work was acceptable to his Lord, praised for what his Lord had charged him with, not falling short in his obedience to Him.
19:56: God Almighty says: And mention, O Muhammad, in this Book of Ours, Idris. He was a man of truth, he did not tell lies, a prophet, to whom We revealed of Our command whatever We willed.
19:57: And We raised him to a high station. It was mentioned that God raised him while he was alive to the fourth heaven. This is the meaning of His statement: And We raised him to a high station, meaning to a place of height and elevation. Some of them said: He was raised to the sixth heaven. Others said: The fourth. The novel mentioned that: Yunus bin Abdul A'la told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Jarir bin Hazim told me, on the authority of Sulayman Al-A'mash, on the authority of Shammar bin Atiyah, on the authority of Hilal bin Yasaf, who said: Ibn Abbas asked Ka'b while I was present, and he said to him: What is the saying of God the Almighty to Idris, And We raised him to a high station? Ka'b said: As for Idris, God revealed to him: I will raise for you every day the equivalent of the deeds of all the children of Adam, so I would like you to increase your deeds. Then a close friend of his from the angels came to him and said: God revealed to me such and such, so the Angel of Death spoke to me, so let him delay me until I increase my deeds. So he carried him between his wings, then he headed with him to the heaven. When he was in the fourth heaven, the Angel of Death met him descending and spoke to the Angel of Death about what Idris had spoken to him about. He said: Where is Idris? He said: He is on my back. The Angel of Death said: It is amazing that I was sent to take the soul of Idris in the fourth heaven, and I kept saying: How can I take his soul in the fourth heaven while he is on earth? So his soul was taken there, and that is what God Almighty said: And We raised him to a high station. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us? And Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: And We raised him to a high station, he said: Idris was raised and did not die, just as Isa was raised. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same, except that he said: And he did not die. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We raised him to a high station. He said: He was raised to the sixth heaven, and he died there. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And We raised him to a high station, that Idris was overtaken by death in the sixth heaven. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, And We raised him to a high station, he said: the fourth heaven. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Harun al-Abdi, on the authority of Abu Saeed al-Khudri: And We raised him to a high station. He said: In the fourth heaven. Ali bin Suhayl narrated: Hajjaj narrated: Abu Ja`far al-Razi narrated: Ar-Rabi` bin Anas narrated: Abu al-`Aliyah al-Riyahi narrated: Abu Hurayrah or someone else - Abu Ja`far al-Razi was not sure - said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was taken on the Night Journey, Gabriel ascended with him to the fourth heaven. He asked to be admitted and it was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. They said: And who is with him? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent to? He said: Yes. They said: May God give him life, he is a brother and a successor. What a good brother, what a good successor, and what a good coming he has been. He said: So he entered and saw a man. He said: This is Idris, may God raise him to a high station. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And We raised him to a high station, he said: Anas bin Malik told us that the Prophet of God was told that when he was taken up to heaven, he said: I came upon Idris in the fourth heaven.
19:58: The Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: These are the ones whose report I have related to you in this Surah, O Muhammad, whom God has blessed with His guidance, so He guided them to the path of righteousness from the prophets from the descendants of Adam, and from the descendants of those whom We carried with Noah in the ark, and from the descendants of Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, and from the descendants of Israel, and from those whom We guided to believe in God and to work in obedience to Him and chose, He says: And from those whom We have chosen and selected for Our message and revelation, so the one who is meant from the descendants of Adam is Idris, and the one who is meant from the descendants of those whom We carried with Noah is Abraham, and the one who is meant from the descendants of Abraham is Isaac, Jacob, and Ishmael, and the one who is meant from the descendants of Israel is Moses, Aaron, Zachariah, Jesus, and his mother Mary, and for this reason the Almighty differentiated their lineages even though He gathers them all with Adam because among them is one who was not from the offspring of the one who was with Noah in the ark, and he is Idris, and Idris is the grandfather of Noah. And the saying of the Most High, When the verses of the Most Gracious are recited to them, meaning: When the proofs and arguments of God that He sent down to them in His books are recited to these prophets whom God has blessed, they fall down in prostration to God, in submission to Him, humility, obedience to His command, and obedience, and weeping, meaning: They fall down in prostration while weeping. Weeping is the plural of weeping, just as ‘ati is the plural of ‘ata, and ‘jathi is the plural of jaath, so it is pluralized and it is fa’ul, just as al-qa’id qu’udan and al-jalis jilusan make it plural. The analogy would have been: and they wept and ‘atwaan, but the waw was disliked after the damma, so it was changed to a ya’, just as it was said in the plural of dalū adlā, and li the plural of bahu abah, and the origin of that is af’al adlu and abhu, so the waw was changed to a ya’ because it came after the damma due to its being too heavy. And there are two widespread dialects for that, and scholars of the reciters of the Qur’an have recited each one of them: they wept and ‘atwaan with the damma, and bkiyan and ‘atyaan with the kasra. It may be possible that crying is crying itself. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab recited Surah Maryam and prostrated and said: This is the prostration, but where is the weeping? He meant: Where is the weeping?
19:59: God Almighty says: Then after those whom I mentioned of the prophets upon whom I bestowed favor, and whose characteristics I described in this surah, there occurred an evil successor who left them on the earth and neglected the prayer. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the description of their wasting the prayer. Some of them said: Their wasting it was their delaying it from its appointed times and their wasting its times. Who said that? Ali bin Saad Al-Kindi told me: Isa bin Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Musa bin Sulayman, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Mukhaymara, regarding his statement, Then there came after them a generation who neglected the prayer, he said: They only neglected the times, and if it had been abandonment, it would have been disbelief. Ishaq bin Zaid Al-Khattabi told us: Al-Faryabi told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Mukhaimira, something similar. Abdul Karim bin Abi Umair told us: Al-Walid bin Muslim told me, on the authority of Abu Amr, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Mukhaimira, who said: They lost the timings, and if they had abandoned them, they would have become infidels because of their abandonment. Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Al-Qasim, something similar. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Isa narrated: Al-Awza’i narrated: Ibrahim bin Yazid narrated: Umar bin Abdul Aziz sent a man to Egypt on an urgent matter for the Muslims. He went out to his guards, and he had previously instructed them not to stand up if they saw him. They made room for him, and he sat among them and said: Who among you knows the man we sent to Egypt? They said: We all know him. He said: Let the youngest of you stand up and leave him. The messenger came to him and said: Do not hurry me, I will tighten my clothes on myself. He came to him and said: Today is Friday, so do not leave until you pray. We have sent you on an urgent matter for the Muslims, so do not hurry what we have sent you for by delaying the prayer from its appointed time, for you will inevitably pray it. Then he recited: “Then there came after them a generation who neglected prayer and pursued desires. So they are going to meet with error.” Then he said: Their waste was not abandoning it, but they wasted time. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abd Al-Rahman and Al-Hasan bin Mas’oud, on the authority of Ibn Mas’oud, that it was said to him: God mentions prayer frequently in the Qur’an: Those who are heedless of their prayers and are constant in their prayers and maintain their prayers. Ibn Mas’oud, may God be pleased with him, said: At its appointed times. They said: We only saw that as neglect. He said: That is disbelief. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Omar Abu Hafs Al-Abar told us, on the authority of Mansour bin Al-Mu'tamir, he said: Masruq said: No one maintains the five prayers, so he is recorded among the heedless, and in their excess is destruction, and their excess is: wasting them from their time. And others said: Rather, their wasting them is: abandoning them. Who said that? Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Abu Sakhr told us, on the authority of Al-Qurazi, that he said regarding this verse, Then there came after them a generation who neglected prayer and pursued desires, meaning: they abandoned prayer. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the two interpretations of this, in my opinion, is the interpretation of the verse, which says: Their wasting it means their abandoning it, because the statement of God, the Most High, after it indicates that this is the case, and that is His statement, the Most High: Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds. So if those whom He described as having wasted it were believers, He would not have excluded from them those who believed and were believers, but they were disbelievers who did not pray to God or perform any obligatory prayer for Him, and they were wicked who preferred their own desires over obeying God. It has been said: Those whom God described with this description are people from this nation who will be at the end of time. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, “Then there came after them a posterity who neglected prayer and pursued desires. So they are going to meet with destruction.” He said: When the Hour comes and the righteous people of the nation of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) go, they will seduce one another in the alleys. Muhammad ibn Amr said: Adultery. Al-Harith said: Adulterers. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly, and he said: Adultery, as Ibn Amr said. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah, Mujahid, and Ata’ bin Abi Rabah, Then there succeeded them a generation the verse, he said: They are the nation of Muhammad. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Ashib told us, he said: Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Tamim bin Muhajir, regarding the statement of God: Then there came after them a generation who neglected the prayer, he said: They are in this nation, they swarm like cattle and donkeys on the roads, they do not fear God in the heavens, nor do they feel shy of people on the earth. As for his saying, They will encounter Ghayān, it means that these successors who came after those prophets whom God bestowed His blessings upon will enter Ghayān, which is the name of a valley in Hell, or the name of a well in it. Abbas bin Abi Talib told me, he said: Muhammad bin Ziyad bin Razan told us, he said: Sharqi bin Qatami told us, on the authority of Luqman bin Amir Al-Khuza’i, he said: I came to Abu Umamah Siddi bin Ajlan Al-Bahili, and I said: Tell us a hadith that you heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: So he called for food, then he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a rock weighing ten ounces were thrown from the edge of Hell, it would not reach its bottom for fifty autumns, then it would end in Ghayyah and Atham. He said: I said: What is Ghayyah and Atham? He said: Two wells at the bottom of Hell in which the pus of the people of Hell flows, and they are the two that God mentioned in His Book: “They neglected the prayer and followed their desires. So they are going to meet Ghayyah,” and His saying in al-Furqan 25:And they do not commit adultery, and whoever does that will meet sin. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Amr bin Asim told us: Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr: Then they will meet Ghayyan meaning: a valley in Hell. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah: Then they will meet with error. He said: A valley in the Fire. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaydah, on the authority of Abdullah, that he said regarding this verse, Then they will meet with error. He said: A river in Hell, foul-tasting and deep in the bottom. Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told me: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of his father, regarding his statement, “Then there came after them a generation who neglected prayer and pursued desires. So they are going to meet with error.” He said: Error is the river of Hell in the Fire, in which those who followed desires are tormented. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of his father, regarding his statement, “Then there came after them a posterity who neglected prayer and pursued desires. So they are going to meet with error.” He said: Error is the river of Hell in the Fire, in which those who followed desires are tormented. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, They neglected the prayer and followed desires, so they are going to meet with error. He said: A river in the Fire into which those who followed desires will be thrown. Others said: Rather, what I meant in this context is: loss. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Then they will meet with error, meaning: loss. Others said: Rather, he meant evil. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Then they will meet with error, he said: Error means evil, and from it is the saying of the poet: Whoever finds good, people praise him for his actions, and whoever goes astray will not lack someone to blame him for his error. Abu Ja`far said: All of these sayings have similar meanings, and that is that whoever visits the two wells mentioned by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the valley mentioned by Ibn Mas`ud in Hell, and enters that, will encounter loss and evil, and that is enough evil for him.
19:60: God the Almighty says: Then these evil successors whose description He described will encounter error, except for those who repent and review the command of God, and believe in Him and His Messenger, and do righteous deeds, meaning: and obey God in what He commanded and forbade, and perform His obligations, and avoid what He has forbidden, for those will enter Paradise, meaning: for those among them in particular will enter Paradise, not those who perished among them due to their disbelief, and their neglect of prayer, and their following of desires. And His statement, and they will not be wronged at all, meaning: and they will not be reduced in the reward for their deeds at all, and they will not be included with those of the evil successors who perished before their repentance from their misguidance, and before their return to obeying their Lord in Hell, but they will enter as the people of faith.
19:61: God the Most High says: Then those will enter Paradise, Gardens of Eden. His saying Gardens of Eden is an accusative translation of Paradise. What He means by His saying Gardens of Eden: gardens of residence. I have explained that previously with its evidence that suffices from repeating it. And His saying which the Most Gracious has promised His servants in the unseen means: These gardens are the gardens which the Most Gracious has promised His believing servants that they will enter in the unseen, because they have not seen them or witnessed them, so they are unseen to them. And His saying Indeed, His promise was fulfilled means, Almighty God the Most High: God's promise was, and His promise in this place is His promise, and it is Paradise that is coming, and His friends and those who obey Him will come to it, whom God will admit into it. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The report came out on the basis that the promise is what is coming, and its meaning is: that it is the one who will come, and he did not say: and his promise was coming, because everything that comes to you, you come to it. And he said: Do you not see that you say: I came upon fifty years, and fifty years came upon me, and all of that is correct. And I have explained the statement about it, and the ha’ in his saying that it is from the mention of the Most Gracious.
19:62: God Almighty says: Those who enter Paradise will not hear therein any idle talk, which is guidance and falsehood of speech and talk, “except peace.” This is from the disconnected exception, and its meaning is: But they will hear peace, which is the angels’ greeting to them. And His statement, And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening, means: And they will have their food and whatever they desire of food and drink in the amount of time in the morning and the amount of time in the evening of the days of this world. Rather, He means that what is between their lunch and their dinner in Paradise is the amount of time between one of us in this world and his dinner, and likewise what is between dinner and lunch, because there is no night or day in Paradise, and this is like His statement, He created the earth in two days and He created the heavens and the earth in six days, meaning by that: of the days of this world. Ali bin Sahl told us: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us: I asked Zuhair bin Muhammad about the statement of God: And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening. He said: There is no night in Paradise. They will be in light forever, and they will have the amount of night and day. They will know the amount of night by the lowering of the veils and the closing of the doors, and they will know the amount of day by the raising of the veils and the opening of the doors. Ali told us, he said: Al-Walid told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Al-Hasan, and he mentioned the gates of Paradise, and he said: Gates whose exterior can be seen from their interior, so speak and speak, and they whisper, Open and close, and you do. Ibn Harb told me: Musa bin Ismail told us: Amer bin Yassaf told us, on the authority of Yahya, who said: The Arabs in their time, if they had dinner and lunch, that was a comfort to them. So God revealed: And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening: the amount of time between your lunch in this world and your evening. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening, he said: When one of the Arabs had lunch and dinner, he was amazed, so God informed them that they would have in Paradise morning and evening, the amount of lunch and dinner. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: It is not morning or evening, but they will be given it according to what they desired in this world. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening, there are two hours in it, morning and evening, for that is for them, there is no night, but rather it is light and brightness.
19:63: God Almighty says: This Paradise, whose description I have described to you, O people, is the Paradise that we will inherit. He says: We will inherit the dwellings of the people of Hell in it. Among Our servants is he who was righteous. He says: he who was fearful of God’s punishment by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins.
19:64: It was mentioned that this verse was revealed because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was slow to receive the revelation from Gabriel. I mentioned some of the narration, and we will mention, God willing, the rest of what we have prepared to mention that we did not mention before. Who said that? Abu Kuraib narrated: Abdullah narrated: Abdullah bin Abaan Al-Ajli, Qubaysah and Wakee’ narrated: Sufyan bin Wakee’ narrated: My father narrated: All of them on the authority of Umar bin Dhir: I heard my father mention on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that Muhammad said to Gabriel: What prevents you from visiting us more often than you visit us? Then this verse was revealed: “And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is in between. And your Lord is not forgetful.” He said: This is the answer to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muhammad bin Muammar told me: Abdul Malik bin Amr told us: Omar bin Dhir told us: My father told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Gabriel: What prevents you from visiting us more often than you do? Then the verse was revealed: We do not descend except by the command of your Lord. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement, And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord to And your Lord is not forgetful. He said: Gabriel was delayed from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was distressed by that and was saddened, so Gabriel came to him and said: O Muhammad, “And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is in between. And your Lord is not forgetful.” Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Gabriel was away from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it seemed as if the Prophet was slow to see him. When he came to him, Gabriel said to him: We do not descend except by the command of your Lord verse. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: “And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us.” He said: This is what Gabriel said. Gabriel was delayed in some of the revelation, so the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You did not come until I missed you. Gabriel said to him: “And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us.” Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, And We do not descend except by the command of your Lord, he said: The statement of the angels when Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked them to pray, is like that in the forenoon. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Gabriel stayed away from Muhammad for twelve nights, and they were saying: Say something. So when he came to him, he said: O Gabriel, you have pitied me so much that the polytheists have suspected every suspicion. Then the verse was revealed: “And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that. And your Lord is not forgetful.” It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord, that He was held back from the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until the polytheists spoke about that, and that was difficult for the Prophet of God, so Gabriel came to him and said: Our being held back from you is difficult for you, and the polytheists speaking about that, but I am only the servant of God and His Messenger, if He commands me to do something I obey Him. And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord, meaning: by the word of your Lord. Then the people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his saying, To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that. Some of them said: By his saying, what is before us, he means the world, and by his saying, what is behind us, he means the Hereafter, and what is between that, the two blasts. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of al-Rabi`: For Him belongs what is before us, meaning the world, and what is behind us, the Hereafter, and what is between that, the two trumpets. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah, he said: What is before us of this world, and what is behind us of the matter of the Hereafter, and what is between that between the two blasts. Others said: What is before us is the Hereafter, what is behind us is this world, and what is between that is between this world and the Hereafter. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Before us is the Hereafter and what is behind us of this world. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: To Him belongs what is before us of the matter of the Hereafter, and what is behind us of the matter of this world, and what is between that between this world and the Hereafter, and your Lord is not forgetful. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: He has what is before us of the Hereafter, and what is behind us of this world, and what is between that between the two blasts. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, what is before us of the Hereafter, and what is behind us of the world. Others said about this: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, What is before us he said: What has passed before us of this world, and what is behind us what will come after us of this world and the Hereafter, and what is between that he said: What is between what has passed before them and what will come after them. Some of the Arab scholars from Basra interpreted this to mean what is before us before we were created, what is behind us after annihilation, and what is between that when we were. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: Its meaning is: He has what is before us of the matter of the Hereafter, because that has not come and has come, so it is before them. For the most common usage of people when they say this matter is before you, is that they mean what has not come and has come, so we said: That is more correct. And what we have left behind of the matter of this world, that is what they left behind and it has passed, so it became behind them by their leaving it behind. And likewise the Arabs say about what a person has passed and what he has left behind, it is behind him and behind him, and what is between that: what is between what has not passed of the matter of this world and the Hereafter, because that is what is between those two times. We said: This is the most appropriate interpretation for it, because this is the most apparent and most likely interpretation, and the interpretation of the Qur’an is based on the most likely of its meanings, unless something prevents it from being accepted. So ponder the statement: Do not be impatient, O Muhammad, for us to be late with you, for we do not descend from the heaven to the earth except by the command of your Lord to descend to it. To God belongs whatever is new of the affairs of the Hereafter that have not yet come and are coming, and whatever has passed and we have left behind of the affairs of this world, and what is between this time and the Day of Resurrection, in His hand is all that, and He is its Owner and Disposer, and none possesses that but Him, so it is not for us to invent a matter in His authority except by His command to us. And your Lord is not forgetful means: And your Lord is not forgetful, so my descent to you is delayed by His forgetting you, rather He is the One from whom nothing in the heaven or on the earth is hidden, so blessed and exalted is He, but He is the Most Knowing of what He manages and decrees in His creation, may His praise be glorified. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, And your Lord is not forgetful. He said: Your Lord has not forgotten you.
19:65: God the Most High says: Your Lord, O Muhammad, is not the Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, because if He had been forgotten, that would not have been right, and he would have perished had it not been for His preservation of him. So the Lord is raised in response to His saying, your Lord. And His saying, Worship Him, means: So adhere to His obedience, and submit to His commands and prohibitions. And be patient in His worship, means: And make yourself patient in carrying out His commands and prohibitions, and working in His obedience, and you will win His pleasure with you, for He is the God who has no equal, no equal, and no likeness in His goodness, generosity, and grace. Do you know of anyone similar to Him? He says: Do you know, O Muhammad, that this Lord whom We have commanded you to worship, and to be patient in obeying Him, has an example in His generosity and munificence, so you worship Him hoping for His grace and bounty without Him? No, that does not exist. And in a similar manner to what we said in interpreting that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Do you know of anyone similar to Him? means: Do you know of an example or likeness for the Lord? Saeed bin Othman Al-Tanukhi told me: Ibrahim bin Mahdi told us, on the authority of Ibad bin Awam, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Amara, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Do you know of anyone similar to Him? He said: Someone similar. Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told me: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding this verse: Do you know of anyone similar to Him? He said: Do you know of anyone similar to Him? Do you know of an example for Him, blessed and exalted be He. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Do you know of anyone with a similar name? God has no similar name nor is He equal to Him. All of His creation acknowledges Him and admits that He is their Creator, and knows that. Then he recites this verse, And if you ask them, ‘Who created them?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’ Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement, Do you know of anyone similar to Him? He said: He says: He has no partner or equal.
19:66: God Almighty says: And man says, the disbeliever who does not believe in resurrection after death: I will be brought out alive so that I may be resurrected after death, after affliction and annihilation! Denying that.
19:67: God Almighty says, Does not man remember? The one who is amazed by this denial of God's ability to revive him after his annihilation, and to bring him into existence after his nonexistence in the creation of himself, that God created him before his death, and created him as a perfect human being from nothing, and he was not before his creation of him, a thing. So he takes that into consideration and knows that the One who created him from nothing is not incapable of bringing him back to life after his death, and bringing him into existence after his annihilation. The reciters differed in their reading of the statement: Or does man not remember? Some of the reciters of Medina and Kufa read it: Or does he not remember with a light dhal. The majority of the reciters of Kufa, Basra and Hijaz read it as or does he not remember with a shaddah on the dhal and the kaf, meaning: or does he not remember. The shaddah is more pleasing to me, although the other is permissible, because the meaning of that is: or does he not think and consider.
19:68: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: By your Lord, O Muhammad, We will surely gather those who say: When we die, will we indeed be brought out alive on the Day of Resurrection from their graves, joined by their allies from among the devils? Then We will surely bring them around Hell on their knees. Al-Jathi is the plural of al-Jathi. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Then We will surely bring them around Hell, kneeling, meaning: sitting, and it is like his statement: And you will see every nation kneeling.
19:69: God Almighty says, Then We will take from every group of them the most rebellious and obstinate against God, and We will begin with them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Aqmar, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, Then We will extract from every sect those of them who are most rebellious against the Most Merciful. He said: We will begin with the greatest, then the greatest in crime. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Then We will surely extract from every sect those of them who were most rebellious against the Most Merciful, meaning: those of them who were most disobedient to the Most Merciful, which is disobeying Him in polytheism. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: Which of them is most rebellious against the Most Merciful? means: disobedient. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us. And Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: From every sect he said: A nation. And his statement: obstinate he said: disbelief. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same, and Ibn Jurayj added to it: So we will begin with them. Abu Jaafar said: The Shiites are the group who cooperate in a matter. It is said of this: the people cooperated, if they cooperated, and from this is their saying to the brave man: he is a Shiite, meaning he is a supporter, so the meaning of the statement is: then we will extract from every group that cooperated in disbelief in God, the most rebellious of them against God, and we will begin by burning him in Hell. And the word shi’i in other than this place means: division? And from this is the statement of God the Almighty: And they were sects meaning: groups, and from this is the statement of Ibn Mas’ud or Sa’d: I hate to come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he says: I have divided my nation. Meaning: I have divided.
19:70: The Almighty says: Then We know better than those whom We remove from every sect who are most deserving of severe punishment and most deserving of great chastisement. It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Jurayj that he used to say about this: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Then We are most knowing of those who are most deserving of it to be burned. He said: Those most deserving of eternal damnation in Hell. Abu Ja`far said: What Ibn Jurayj said is a meaningless statement, because God, the Most High, mentioned that those whom He removes from every sect of the infidels are the most severe in disbelief, and there is no doubt that there is no disbeliever in God except that he will abide eternally in the Fire, so there is no reason, and all of them will abide eternally in Hell, for it to be said: Then We know best those who are more deserving of eternal life than these immortals, but the meaning of that is what we mentioned, and it may be possible that it means: Then We know best those who are more deserving of some of the levels of Hell, salaan. As-Sali is the infinitive of salita tasalla salaan, and as-Sali is fa`ul, but its waw was changed to a ya’ and was assimilated into the ya’ that comes after it, which is the lam of the verb, so it became a shaddah ya’.
19:71: God Almighty says: There is not one of you, O people, but will pass over to Hell. It was incumbent upon your Lord, O Muhammad, that they should pass over to it, a decree already decreed. He has decreed that and made it obligatory in the Mother of the Book. Scholars differed about the meaning of the word Wurood that God mentioned in this place. Some of them said: Entering. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated: Abd al-Razzaq narrated: Ibn Uyaynah narrated on the authority of Amr: Someone told me that heard Ibn Abbas arguing with Nafi’ bin al-Azraq. Ibn Abbas said: Wurood means entering. Nafi’ said: No. Ibn Abbas recited: “Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell. You will be entering it.” Was he entering it or not? And he said: He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire, and wretched is the place to be entered. Was he entering it or not? As for you and I, we will enter it, so see if we will emerge from it or not. And I do not see that God will bring you out of it by denying you.” Nafi’ laughed. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Hajjaj narrated: On the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, who said: Abu Rashid Al-Haruri said: They mentioned this and Al-Haruri said: They do not hear its hissing. Ibn Abbas said: Woe to you, are you crazy? Where is the saying of God Almighty: He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and will lead them into the Fire - and wretched is the place they are led to, “And We will drive the criminals to Hell in droves,” and His saying: And there is not one of you but will pass over it, and by God, if the supplication of those who have passed away was: O God, take me out of the Fire unharmed and admit me into Paradise victorious. Ibn Jurayj said: He says: The arrivals that God mentioned in the Qur’an: the entrance, so that every righteous and wicked person may enter it in the Qur’an, four arrivals: Then He will lead them into the Fire, “And gravel of Hell, you will be entering it,” And We will drive the criminals to Hell in droves, and His saying: And there is not one of you but will pass over it. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: “And there is not one of you but will pass over it: this is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed.” He knows the righteous and the wicked. Have you not heard the statement of God Almighty to Pharaoh: He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and will lead them into the Fire, and wretched is the place they are led to. And He said: And We will drive the criminals to Hell, in droves. So He called entering the Fire entering, not going out. Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Bakkar bin Abi Marwan, on the authority of Khalid bin Ma’dan, who said: The people of Paradise said after they entered Paradise: Did not our Lord promise us to pass through the Fire? He said: You passed by it while it was extinguished. Ibn Arafa said: Marwan bin Muawiyah said: Bakkar bin Abi Marwan said, or he said: solid. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Marhum ibn Abd al-Aziz told us: Abu Imran al-Joni told us, on the authority of Abu Khalid, who said: The earth will be a fire one day, so what have you prepared for it? He said: That is what God said: “And there is not one of you but will pass over it: this is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed. Then We will save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees.” Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Al-Saleel, on the authority of Ghanim ibn Qays, he said: They mentioned the arrival of the Fire, so Ka’b said: The Fire will be held by the people as if it were the back of a sack, until the feet of all creatures, both the righteous and the wicked, will be level on it. Then a crier will call out to it: Hold back your companions, and leave my companions. He said: Then every guardian of it will be swallowed up, and it knows them better than a man knows his own son, and the believers will emerge with their bodies fresh. He said: And Ka’b said: From what is between the shoulders of the treasurer of its treasurers is a year’s journey, with each one of them is a column with two branches, with which he pushes, and with it seven hundred thousand will be thrown into the Fire. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Malik ibn Mughul, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: Whenever Abu Maysarah went to bed, he would say: I wish my mother had not given birth to me. Then he would cry. It was said: What makes you cry, Abu Maysarah? He said: He told us that we were entering it, but he did not tell us that we were leaving it. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Qais, who said: Abdullah bin Rawaha cried during his illness, and his wife cried too. He said: What makes you cry? She said: I saw you crying, so I cried too. Ibn Rawaha said: I know that I will enter Hell, but I do not know whether I will be saved from it or not. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Amr Dawud bin Al-Zubayr told us, he said: I heard Al-Suddi mentioning on the authority of Marra Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, And there is not one of you but will pass over it, he said: enter it. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And there is not one of you but will pass over it, he said: He will enter it. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim, who said: Abdullah bin Rawahah had his head on his wife’s lap, and he cried, so his wife cried. He said: What makes you cry? She said: I saw you crying, so I cried. He said: I remembered the words of God, There is not one of you but will pass over it, and I do not know whether I will be saved from it or not. Others said: Rather, it is bitter. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And there is not one of you but will pass over it, meaning Hell, which people will pass over. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And there is not one of you but will pass over it, he said: He is the one who passes by it. Khallad bin Aslam told us: An-Nadr told us: Israel told us: Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah, regarding His statement, There is not one of you but will pass over it, he said: The path over Hell is like the edge of a sword. The first layer will pass like lightning, the second like the wind, the third like the best of horses, and the fourth like the best of beasts. Then they will pass and the angels will say, O God, save, save. Others said: Rather, the arrival is the entry, but he meant the infidels, not the believers. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Dawud told us: Shu’bah told us: Abdullah bin Al-Sa’ib told me, on the authority of a man who heard Ibn Abbas recite it: And there is not one of you but will pass over it, meaning the disbelievers. He said: No believer will pass over it. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Amr bin al-Walid al-Shani told us: I heard Ikrimah say: There is not one of you but will pass over it, meaning the infidels. Others said: Rather, the entrance is general for every believer and disbeliever, except that the entrance of the believer is passing through, and the entrance of the disbeliever is entering. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And there is not one of you but will pass over it, the Muslims’ passing over the bridge between its two sides and the polytheists’ passing over it to enter it. He said: And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The men and women who slip on that day will be many, and two rows of angels will surround the bridge, and their supplication on that day will be: O God, save, save. Others said: The believer will suffer from fever and illness in this world. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Aswad, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Fever is the portion of every believer from the Fire. Then he recited: And there is not one of you but will pass over it. Imran bin Bakkar Al-Kila’i told me: Abu Al-Mughira told us: Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid bin Tamim told us: Ismail bin Ubaid God told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to visit a man from among his companions who had an illness, and I was with him. Then he said: God says: It is My Fire which I unleash upon My believing servant so that it may be his portion of the Fire in the Hereafter. Others said: Everyone will return it, then the believers will issue from it with their deeds. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, who said: Al-Suddi told us, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah: And there is not one of you but will pass over it. He said: They will pass over it and then depart from it with their deeds. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Mahdi told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, something similar. Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Maharbi told me: Asbat told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Ubayd God, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: I was with Ibn Abbas when a man called Abu Rashid, who was Nafi’ ibn al-Azraq, came to him and said to him: O Ibn Abbas, what do you think of the statement of God, “And there is not one of you but will pass over it: this is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed.” He said: As for you and me, O Abu Rashid, we will pass over it, so see if we will depart from it or not. Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Asim told us: Ibn Jurayj told us: Abu al-Zubayr told me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdullah being asked about the roses, and he said: On the Day of Resurrection, we will be on windows or skylights, above the people, and the nations will be called with their idols and what they used to worship, one after the other, and they will be taken away and they will follow him. He said: And every person, hypocrite and believer, will be given a light, and darkness will cover them, then they will follow him. And on the bridge of Hell will be hooks that will seize whomever God wills, and the light of the hypocrite will be extinguished, and the believers will be saved, and the first group will be saved like the moon on the night of the full moon, and seventy thousand will not be held accountable, then those who follow them will be like the brightest star in the sky, then likewise, then intercession will be established and they will intercede, and whoever said there is no god but God and in whose heart is the weight of a barley grain of goodness will be taken out of the Fire, then they will be thrown towards Paradise, and the people of Paradise will pour water over them, and they will grow like something growing in a flood, then they will be asked and they will be given the world and ten times its like. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Al-Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: A man said to his brother: Has it come to you that you will enter Hell? He said: Yes. He said: Has it come to you that you will leave it? He said: No. He said: Then why are you laughing? He said: So he was not seen laughing until he met God. Yunus narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, he said: Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to us that Bakir narrated to him that he said to Basr ibn Sa`id: So-and-so says: The entrance to Hellfire is standing on it. Basr said: As for Abu Hurairah, I heard him say: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the people will gather and a crier will call out: Let each group join what they used to worship. So one will stand towards a stone, another towards a horse, and another towards a piece of wood, until only those who worshipped God remain. God will come to them, and when they see Him, they will stand towards Him. He will take them and lead them on the Sirat, and in it will be burning bushes. At that time, the call to intercession will be made, and the people will pass by, and the prophets will say: O God, save, save. Bakir said: Ibn `Umairah used to say: Then a Muslim will be saved, and another will be upside down in Hell and scratched, then another will be saved. The most correct of the sayings is the one that says: Everyone will return to it, then the believers will emerge from it, and God will save them, and the disbelievers will fall into it. Their arrival into it is what the reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, have shown about their passing over the bridge erected over the surface of Hell, with a Muslim being saved and one being piled up in it. Mentioning the report narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding this: Abu Kuraib narrated: Ibn Idris narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Umm Mubashar, the wife of Zayd ibn Haritha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said while he was in Hafsa’s house: No one who witnessed Badr and Al-Hudaybiyyah will enter the Fire. Hafsa said: O Messenger of God, does not God say, ‘There is not one of you but will pass over it’? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Then God will save those who feared God. Al-Hasan bin Mudrik told us: Yahya bin Hammad told us: Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Umm Mubashar, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly. Abu Kuraib told us: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Umm Mubashar, on the authority of Hafsah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I hope that no one who witnessed Badr and Al-Hudaybiyyah will enter the Fire. She said: I said: O Messenger of God, does not God say: There is not one of you but will pass over it? He said: Did you not hear Him say: Then We will save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees? Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq: Ubaydullah ibn al-Mughira ibn Mu'ayqib told me, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Amr ibn Abd al-'Atwari, one of the Banu Laith, who was in the care of Abu Sa'id. He said: I heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: "The bridge will be placed between the two sides of Hell, and there will be thorns on it like the thorns of the Sa'dan tree. Then people will seek passage, and some will be saved, some will be wounded by it, some will be saved, some will be detained, and some will be piled up in it. Then, when God has finished judging between His servants, the believers will miss men who were with them in this world, praying as they pray, paying their zakat, fasting as they fast, performing the pilgrimage as they do, and fighting as they do. They will say: 'O our Lord, there are servants from among Your servants who were with us in this world, praying as we pray, paying our zakat, fasting as we fast, performing the pilgrimage as we do, and fighting as we do. We do not see them. Then He will say: 'Go to the Fire.' So they will bring them out, and they will find that the Fire has seized them according to their deeds. Some of them will be seized up to their feet, some up to half of their shins, some up to their knees, some up to their breasts, and some up to their necks, but their faces will not be covered. So they will extract them from it and throw them into the Water of Life. It was said: What is the Water of Life, O Messenger of God? He said: The people of Paradise will be washed, and they will grow as a plant grows in the scum of a torrent. Then the prophets will intercede for everyone who testified sincerely that there is no god but God, and they will extract them from it. Then God will bestow His mercy upon those in it, and He will not leave in it a servant in whose heart there is an atom’s weight of faith except that He will bring him out of it.” Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told me: My father and Shu`ayb ibn al-Layth told us, on the authority of al-Layth ibn Khalid, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of `Ata’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The bridge will be brought - meaning on the Day of Resurrection - and will be placed between the two sides of Hell. We said: O Messenger of God, what is the bridge? He said: A flat, slippery place, with hooks and claws on it and flattened thorns with curved spikes that lead to Najd, called al-Sa`dan. The believers will pass over it like lightning and wind, and like the best horses and riders. One Muslim will be saved, another Muslim will be scratched, and another will be crushed in Hell. Then the last of them will pass, dragged. You will not be more fervent in your plea to me for the truth, which has become clear to you, than the believers on that day to the Almighty, Blessed and Exalted, when they see that they have been saved and their brothers have remained.” Ahmad bin Isa told me: Saeed bin Katheer bin Ufayr told us, on the authority of Malik: Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, who said: I asked Jabir bin Abdullah about the entrance, and he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “It is the entrance. They will enter the Fire until they emerge from it, and the last one to remain will be a man on the Sirat, crawling, and God will raise a tree for him. He said: He will say: O Lord, bring me closer to it. He said: So God, the Blessed and Exalted, will bring him closer to it. He said: Then he will say: O Lord, admit me to Paradise. He said: He will say: Ask. He said: So he will be asked. He said: He will say: That is for you and ten times that or something like that? He said: He will say: O Lord, are you mocking me? He said: So he will laugh until his uvula and molars are visible.” Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yahya ibn Ayoubih told me, and Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Rushdin, all of them, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Fa’id, on the authority of Sahl ibn Mu’adh, on the authority of his father, “on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Whoever guards behind the Muslims in the way of God voluntarily, and the ruler does not seize him by guarding, he will not see the Fire with his own eyes except by fulfilling the oath, for God Almighty says: ‘There is not one of you but will pass over it.’” Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us: Al-Zuhri told me, on the authority of Ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has three things die, the Fire will not touch him except for the oath meaning: the watering place. As for his saying: It was a decree that was decreed by your Lord, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of it. Some of them said that its meaning is: It was a decree that was decreed by your Lord. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: Inevitably he said: Fate. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: It is a decreed event. He said: It is a decree. Others said: Rather, its meaning is: It was an obligatory oath upon your Lord. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Amr Dawud bin Al-Zubayr told us, he said: I heard Al-Suddi mentioning on the authority of Marra Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, It was a decree that was decreed upon your Lord. He said: An obligatory oath. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: It was a decree that was decreed upon your Lord. He said: an obligatory oath. Abu Jaafar said: I have explained the statement on that.
19:72: God the Most High says: Then We will save from the Fire after they have all entered it, those who feared Him and feared Him, by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience. And We will leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees. God the Most High says: And We will leave those who wronged themselves, so they worshipped other than God, disobeyed their Lord, and went against His commands and prohibitions, in the Fire. On their knees, meaning: kneeling on their knees. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And He will leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: And He will leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And He will leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees, he said: The kneeling is the worst of sitting. A man does not sit on his knees except when distress befalls him. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Then We will save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees, that people will enter Hell while it is equal and dark. As for the believers, their good deeds will shine for them, so they will be saved from it. As for the disbelievers, their deeds will destroy them, and they will be detained because of their sins.
19:73: God the Almighty says: And when Our verses which We sent down to Our Messenger Muhammad are recited to the people as clear proofs, meaning clear to whoever contemplates them and thinks about them that they are evidence for what God made them evidence for for His servants, those who disbelieved in God and His Book and His verses, and they are the Quraysh, say to those who believed and affirmed it, and they are the companions of Muhammad, Which of the two parties is better in position? He means by position: their place of residence, which is their dwellings and homes, and better in company, which is the assembly, it is said from it: I gathered the people, I gathered them in a assembly, and it is said: he is in the assembly of his people and in their club: meaning the same, and from the assembly Hatim said: I was invited to the first assembly, but he did not look at me with squinting eyes. The interpretation of the words: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say to those who believe: Which of the two parties - us and you - has more spacious life, more comfortable life, better dwelling, better assembly, and more numerous and more omnipresent in assembly - us or you? And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, The best place to stay and the best place to gather. He said: The place is the home, and the gathering is the assembly. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, ‘Which of the two parties is better in position and better in company?’ He said: The place of residence is the dwelling place, and the assembly is the council, the blessings and the joy in which they were, and it is as God said to the people of Pharaoh when He destroyed them and narrated their story in the Qur’an, saying, How many gardens and springs did they leave behind, and crops and noble dwellings, and comfort in which they used to rejoice. (al-Dukhan 44:5-6) So the place of residence is the place of residence and the assembly is the council and gathering in which they used to gather. And God said in what He narrated to His Messenger regarding the matter of Lot when He said, And you commit evil in your assemblies. (al-Ankabut 29:29). The Arabs call the assembly: the club. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, and the best company, means a gathering. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Which of the two parties? He said: Quraysh say it to the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the best company. He said: Their gatherings, they also say it. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, ‘Which of the two parties is better in position and better in company?’ They saw the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their rough living, and among them were harshness, so the polytheists presented what you hear his statement, and better in company, meaning: a gathering. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Which of the two parties is better in position and better in company? He said: The company is the assembly. And he recited the statement of God Almighty, Then let him call his assembly (al-Alaq 96:7), and he said: His assembly.
19:74: God Almighty says: And how many have We destroyed before these, O Muhammad, those who said to the believers, when the verses of the Most Gracious were recited to them, which of the two groups is better in position, and better in company, and whose councils are better than those of a generation, and whose dwellings are more comfortable than these, and whose appearance is better than theirs, and whose forms are more beautiful. So We destroyed their wealth, and changed their forms. And from that is the saying of Alqamah bin Abdah: A dead man, the color of purple, I spread out to sell the worn-out in cubic flint. By Swan means: the bed in which clothes are kept. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Abu Abbas: The best furniture and appearance. He said: The appearance is the appearance, and the furniture is the goods. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The vision is the sight. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, the best in furniture and appearance, meaning: in appearance. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The best furniture and appearance. Furniture means money, and appearance means sight. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Hudha told us, he said: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, furniture and property, he said: Furniture is the best of goods, and property, he said: money. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, God Almighty says: And how many generations before them have We destroyed who were better in furnishings and appearance: meaning more enjoyment and a better position and settlement, so God destroyed their wealth and corrupted their images for them, Almighty and Exalted. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, the most beautiful furniture and appearance, he said: the most beautiful image and the most wealth. Muhammad Bani Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Furnishment he said: the goods, and vision he said: in what people see. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Ibn Hamid and Bishr bin Muadh told us: Jarir bin Qabus told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Furniture means money, and the view means a beautiful appearance. Al-Qasim told us: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And they were seen as a sight in color and beauty. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, The best furniture and appearance, he said: The appearance is the view, and the furniture is the furnishings, the best furnishings, and the best appearance. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say regarding his statement, the best furniture, meaning money, and appearance, meaning: the beautiful view. The reciters differed in reading this, so the majority of the reciters of the people of Medina read it as wariya without a hamza, and if it is read in this way, it has two meanings: One of them is that the reciter intended the hamza, so he replaced it with a ya, so the ya that was replaced from the hamza and the ya that is the lam of the verb came together, so they were assimilated, and they became one doubled ya to make it similar, since it was the beginning of a verse, to its counterparts from all the beginnings of verses before and after it. The other is that it is from ruwayt arwi ruwayt wa riya, and if that is intended by it, the meaning of the statement is: And how many generations before them did We destroy, who were better in provision, better in looking after their wealth, and better in knowing how to manage it, because the Arabs say: How good is the vision of so-and-so in this matter if he had good insight into it and knowledge of it. The majority of the reciters of Iraq, Kufa, and Basra read it as wariya with a hamza, meaning: the vision of the eye, as if he meant: the best provision and mirror. It was narrated that some of them read: The best furniture and clothing, with a z, as if he meant the best furnishings, appearance, and view. This is because the cloth is the appearance and view from their saying: I decorated the girl, meaning: I adorned her and made her look good. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the readings in this regard is the reading of the one who reads athathan wa ru`ya with the ra’ and the hamza, because of the consensus of the hujjat from the people of interpretation that its meaning is: the view, and that is from seeing with the eye, not from seeing, so therefore the hamzat is more appropriate for it. If a reader reads it without the hamza, and he means this meaning, then he is not mistaken in his reading. As for his reading with the zay, then it is a reading outside the reading of the readers, so I do not permit reading with it because it is contrary to their reading, even though they have a correct interpretation. The Arab scholars differed as to whether a single word for athath is plural or singular. Al-Ahmar, as he was told, said: It is the plural of the singular word aathathah, just as the singular word for hamam is the plural of hamama, and the singular word for sahab is the plural of sahabah. As for Al-Farra’, he used to say: It has no singular, just as mataa’ has no singular. He said: The Arabs pluralize mataa’ as amaghtah, “amati’,” and mataa’. Qala’ said: If you had pluralized athath, you would have said: three athah and athath. As for ra’i, its plural is ra’a.
19:75: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who say, when Our verses are recited to them: Which of the two parties, from us and from you, is better in position and better in company? Whoever from us and from you is in error, deviating from the path of truth, taking a path other than that of guidance, then let the Most Merciful extend for him a period. He says: Let God prolong his error for him, and let him have respite in it. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, In error, then let the Most Merciful extend for him a term, then let God leave him in his transgression.
