Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. And His statement, Until when they see what they are promised, either the punishment or the Hour, God Almighty says: Say to them: Whoever among us and among you is in error, let the Most Merciful prolong his error until God’s command comes to them, either an immediate punishment, or they meet their Lord at the establishment of the Hour which God has promised His creation that He will gather them for. For when God’s promise of one of these two matters comes to them, they will know who is worse in position and dwelling than you and them and weaker in soldiers, are they or you? And then they will know which of the two groups is better in position and better in company.
19:76: God Almighty says: And God increases the one who follows the straight path, and is guided to the path of righteousness, so he believes in his Lord, and believes in His verses, and does what He commands him to do, and refrains from what He forbids him from, guidance through what he rereport of faith in the obligations that He imposes upon him, and he acknowledges the necessity of imposing them upon him, and he works with them, so that is an increase from God in his guidance by His verses, guidance upon His guidance, and that is similar to His saying: And when a surah is revealed, some of them say, ‘Which of you has this increased in faith?’ As for those who believe, it increases them in faith, and they rejoice. (al-Tawbah 9:124) Some of them interpreted this as: And God increases those who are guided in guidance by the abrogating and abrogated verses of the Qur’an, so he believes in the abrogating verse, just as he believed in the abrogated verse before. This is an increase in guidance from God to him in addition to his previous guidance. And the lasting good deeds are better with your Lord as reward. God the Most High says: “And the deeds that God has commanded His servants to do and is pleased with from them, the lasting good deeds for them, not the transient ones, are better with your Lord as a reward for their people. “And better as a return” for them than the positions of these polytheists and their clubs that they boast about over the people of faith in this world. We have explained the meaning of the lasting good deeds, and we have mentioned the differences of opinion among those who differ on this, and we have demonstrated the correctness of what is said about it in the past, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated: Abd al-Razzaq narrated: Umar bin Rashid narrated: Yahya bin Abi Katheer narrated: Abu Salamah bin Abd al-Rahman bin Awf narrated: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat down one day and took a dry stick, crushed its leaves and then said: ‘Saying La ilaha illa God, Allahu Akbar, al-Hamdulillah, and subhan God erases sins, just as the wind erases the leaves of this tree. Take them, O Abu al-Darda’, before you are prevented from them. They are the lasting good deeds, and they are from the treasures of Paradise.’” Abu Salamah said: Whenever Abu al-Darda’ mentioned this hadith, he would say: ‘I will glorify God, declare His greatness, and praise God, until when an ignorant person sees me, he will think I am crazy.’”
19:77: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Have you seen, O Muhammad, the one who disbelieved in Our signs and did not believe in them and denied Our threat from the people of disbelief and said, while he was a disbeliever in God and in His Messenger, ‘I will surely be given wealth and children’ in the Hereafter?” He mentioned that these verses were revealed about Al-‘As ibn Wa’il Al-Sahmi Abu ‘Amr ibn Al-‘As. The novel mentioned that: Abu Al-Sa'ib and Sa'id bin Yahya narrated: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated on the authority of Al-A'mash on the authority of Muslim on the authority of Masruq on the authority of Khabbab who said: I was a blacksmith, and Al-'As bin Wa'il owed me a debt. I came to him to collect it, but he said: By God, I will not pay you until you disbelieve in Muhammad. I said: By God, I will not disbelieve in Muhammad until you die and are resurrected. He said: So he said: So if I die and am resurrected as you say, you come to me with wealth and children. He said: Then God revealed: Have you seen he who disbelieved in Our verses and said, 'I will surely be given wealth and children?' Has he known the unseen, or has he taken a covenant from the Most Merciful?... until His saying: and he comes to Us alone. Abu Al-Saib told me about it, and he read in the hadith: And a child. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn `Abbas: Some men from among the companions of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) were seeking a debt from Al-`As ibn Wa`il As-Sahmi, so they came to him to collect it. He said: Do you not claim that in Paradise there is silver, gold, silk, and all kinds of fruits? They said: Yes. He said: Your appointed time is in the Hereafter, and by God, I will be given wealth and children, and I will be given the like of the book that you brought. So God gave an example of it in the Qur’an, and said: Have you seen he who disbelieved in Our verses and said, ‘I will certainly be given wealth’... until His saying: and he will come to Us alone. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, I will be given wealth and children, he said: Al-Amir bin Wa’il says it. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr bin Muadh narrated: Yazid narrated: Saeed narrated: Qatada said: His statement, Have you seen he who disbelieved in Our verses and said, ‘I will surely be given wealth and children,’ He mentioned to us that some men from among the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to a polytheist man to collect a debt from him. He said: Doesn’t your companion claim that there is silk and gold in Paradise? They said: Yes. He said: Then your appointment is Paradise. By God, I will not believe in the book that you have brought - mocking the Book of God - and I will be given wealth and children.
19:78: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated: Abd al-Razzaq narrated: Ath-Thawri narrated: Al-A'mash narrated: Abu al-Duha narrated: Masruq narrated: Khabbab bin al-Arat said: I was a blacksmith in Mecca, and I worked for al-'As bin Wa'il. I owed him money, so I came to collect it from him, but he said to me: I will not pay you until you disbelieve in Muhammad. I said: I will not disbelieve in Muhammad until you die and are resurrected. He said: Then when I am resurrected, I will have wealth and children. I mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: Have you seen he who disbelieved in Our verses and said, 'I will surely be given wealth and children'? to and he will come to Us alone. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, and a son. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the people of Kufa, read it as and a son with a fat-ha on the waw from son in the entire Qur’an. However, Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ specifically mentioned the one in Surat Nuh with a damma, so he read it as his wealth and his son (Nuh: 21). As for the majority of the reciters of Kufa, other than Asim, they read from this surah from His statement, wealth and son to the end of the surah, and the two in Az-Zukhruf, and the one in Nuh, with a damma and a sukoon on the lam. The Arabists differed about the meaning of this if its waw is closed. Some of them said: It is the same to have a closed and a open, but they are two languages, like their saying al-‘adām and al-‘adām, and al-ḥuzn and al-ḥuzn. They cited as evidence for their saying the following poet’s saying: I wish so-and-so was in his mother's womb, and I wish so-and-so was the son of a donkey. Al-Harith bin Halza says: I have seen people who have produced wealth and children. And the saying of Ru'bah: Praise be to God, the Almighty, the One, Who has not taken from a son a son. And the Arabs say in a similar way: Your son is from my blood, your descendants. He said: And all of this is one, meaning son. And it was mentioned to me that Qais makes son a plural, and son is one. Perhaps those who read it with the dammah in what they chose in it, only read it that way to differentiate between the plural and the one. Abu Ja`far said: What is more correct than what I say about this is that the fat-ha in the waw of al-walad and the damma in it have the same meaning, and they are two languages, so whichever one the reader reads with, he is correct, except that the fat-ha is the more famous of the two languages in it, so reading with it is more pleasing to me for that reason. And His statement, He has knowledge of the unseen, means, the Almighty says: This speaker of this statement has knowledge of the unseen, so he knows that he will have wealth and children in the Hereafter by being informed of the knowledge of what is hidden from him. Or has he taken a covenant from the Most Merciful? He says: Or has he believed in God and done what He commanded him to do, and refrained from what He forbade him from doing, so that he has a covenant with God that He will give him what he said of wealth and children. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, Has he known the unseen or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful? with a good deed he had done.
19:79: God the Most High means by His saying: No, that is not the case. He did not know the unseen, so He knew the truth of what he says, and the reality of what he mentions, nor did he take a covenant with the Most Merciful to believe in God and His Messenger, and to work in obedience to Him, but rather he lied and disbelieved. Then God the Most High said: We will record what he says: meaning, We will record what this disbeliever says about his Lord, who says, I will surely be given wealth and children, and We will extend for him a great deal of punishment: meaning, We will increase his punishment in Hell for his false and invalid speech in this world, in addition to his punishment for his disbelief in God.
19:80: And His saying, And We will inherit from him what he says, the Almighty says: And We will deprive this speaker: I will be given in the Hereafter wealth and children, his wealth and children, and his wealth and children will be ours without him, and he will come to us on the Day of Resurrection alone, with no wealth or children with him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa H told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, And We inherit from him what he says: his wealth and his children, and that is what Al-Aasi bin Wa’il said. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We will inherit from him what he says, and he will come to Us alone, meaning he has no money or children. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And We will inherit from him what he says, he said: What he has. And what! His statement, I will be given wealth and children, and in the wording of Ibn Masoud: And We will inherit from him what he has. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And We will inherit from him what he says, he said: What he collected from the world and what he did in it. He said, And he comes to us alone. He said, One of those, not followed by a few or many. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And We inherit from him what he says: We inherit from him.
19:81: God the Almighty says: And O Muhammad, these polytheists from your people have taken gods to worship besides God, so that these gods may be a source of honor for them, protecting them from the punishment of God, and they take their worship of them as a means of nearness to God. And His saying, No, God the Almighty says: The matter is not as they thought and hoped from these gods that they worship besides God, that they will save them from the punishment of God, and deliver them from it, and from the evil that their Lord intended for them. And His saying, They will disbelieve in their worship, God the Almighty says: But the gods will disbelieve in the Hereafter because of the worship of these polytheists on the Day of Resurrection, and their disbelief in it is their saying to their Lord: We disavow to You that they used to worship us, so they denied that they worshipped them or ordered them to do so, and they disavowed them, and that is their disbelief in their worship.
19:82: As for his saying, And they will be against them, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: And their gods will be a help to them. And they said: The opposite means the help. Who said that? Ali told us, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, and they will be against them, meaning: helpers. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa H told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And they will be against them, he said: A helper against them, quarreling with them and lying to them. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, And they will be against them, he said: Their idols will be in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. Others said: Rather, he meant the opposite in this place: the peers. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And they will be opponents to them, meaning: they will be companions to them. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, and they will be opponents to them, they will be companions in the Fire, cursing each other and disowning each other. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement opposite, he said: Companions in the Fire. Others said: The meaning of the opposite here is: the enemy. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And they will be opponents to them, he said: Enemies. Others said: The meaning of the opposite in this place is: affliction. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, and they will be against them, he said: They will be a calamity against them. The opposite is the calamity, and the opposite in the speech of the Arabs is: disagreement. It is said: So-and-so opposes so-and-so in such-and-such, if he disagrees with him in his actions, so he spoils what he has corrected, and corrects what he has corrupted. And since that is its meaning, and the gods of these polytheists whom God mentioned in this place disavow them, and deny them on that day, they became their opposites, and they were described as such. The Arabists differed about the reason for unifying the opposite, which is an attribute of a group. Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: wahad because it can be a group and one, like rasad and arsad. He said: rasad can also be for a group. Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: wahad because its meaning is helper, and he mentioned that Abu Nahik used to read it that way. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Yahya bin Wadh told us, he said: Abdul-Mumin told us, he said: I heard Abu Nahik Al-Azdi reading No, they will disbelieve, meaning all the gods will disbelieve in their worship.
19:83: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Have you not seen, O Muhammad, that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers in God? To incite them means to move them by tempting and misleading them, so they disturb them to commit God’s sins and tempt them with them until they commit them. To incite means to incite and tempt. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told us, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying Aza means: He tempts them with temptation. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: “You incite the disbelievers to polytheism. Go ahead, go ahead with this matter until you cause them to fall into the Fire. Go ahead with error, go ahead.” Abu Kuraib told us: Abu Idris told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement, You tempt them with temptation, he said: You tempt them with temptation. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, It disturbs them with disturbance, he said: It disturbs them with disturbance in disobeying God. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Ibn Uthma told us: Saeed bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding God’s statement, It drives them to disobey God, he said: It drives them to disobey God. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, You will disturb them with a disturbance, he said: You will disturb them with a disturbance in disobeying God. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Have you not seen that We send the devils upon the disbelievers, to incite them with [a] great incitement? Then he recited, And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful - We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion. (al-Zukhruf 43:36), he said: Incite them with [a] great incitement, he said: “He drives them to pieces to disobey God Almighty, and tempts them to do it, as a person tempts another to do something. It is said from this: I incited so-and-so to do such-and-such,” if you tempted him with it, I incite him with a great incitement and a great incitement, and I heard the sizzling of the pot: which is the sound of it boiling on the fire. From this is the hadith of Mutraf from his father, that he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was praying, and there was a sizzling sound in his stomach like the sizzling of a cauldron.
19:84: And His statement, "So do not hasten upon them. We are only preparing for them a [decreed] number." The Almighty says: So do not hasten upon these disbelievers by seeking punishment and destruction for them, O Muhammad. We are only preparing for them a [decreed] number. He says: We only delay their destruction so that they may increase in sin, and We count all their deeds and enumerate them, even their very breaths, so that We may reward them for all of them. We did not leave their destruction untimely for any good that We intended for them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told us, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, We only count for them a count, meaning: their breaths that they take in this world, so they are counted like their years and their life spans.
19:85: God the Most High says: The Day We shall gather those who feared Him in this world and feared His punishment, so they avoided His disobedience and performed His duties to their Lord. As a delegation, meaning by delegation: the riders. It is said: I came to someone if you went to him. And the people sent a delegation to their leader if they sent an expedition from before them. And the delegation in this place means gathering, but it is singular because it is a source and their singular is wafid. And the delegation may be plural: delegations, as some of the Banu Hanifa said: I am praising what the head of the delegations, Muzahim bin Jassas, is doing. In this case, delegations may be the plural of delegate, just as sitting is the plural of sitting. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Ishaq, on the authority of al-Nu’man bin Sa’d, on the authority of Ali, regarding His statement, On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation, he said: By God, the delegation will not be gathered on their feet, nor will they be driven in a cart, but they will be brought she-camels the likes of which mankind has never seen, on which are saddles of gold and their reins are of emerald, and they will ride on them until they knock on the gates of Paradise. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu Hurairah: On the Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation. He said: On camels. Ali told us, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation, meaning: as riders. Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us: Amr bin Qais Al-Mala’i told us: When the believer emerges from his grave, he will be met by the most beautiful image and the most fragrant. He will say: Do you recognize me? He will say: No, except that God made your scent pleasant and your image beautiful. He will say: That is how I was in this world. I was your righteous deeds. As long as I rode you in this world, ride me today. And he recited: The Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, To the Most Gracious a delegation. He said: A delegation to Paradise. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement, On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation, he said: On the best of horses. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: I heard Sufyan al-Thawri say: On the Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation. He said: On camels, female camels.
19:86: And His statement, And We will drive the criminals to Hell, thirsty. God Almighty says: And We will drive the disbelievers in God who committed crimes to Hell, thirsty. And the word flow is a noun derived from the saying of the speaker: I brought such-and-such, I brought it flowing, and for this reason it was not pluralized, and it was described by the word shaddah as a plural. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told me, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And We will drive the criminals to Hell, thirsty, meaning: thirsty. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu Hurairah: And We will drive the criminals to Hell, thirsty. He said: Thirsty. Yaqub and Al-Fadl bin Sabah told me: Ismail bin Aliyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, who said: I heard Al-Hasan say regarding His statement, And We will drive the criminals to Hell, thirsty. He said: Thirsty. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the same. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, to Hell in a state of thirst, he said: thirsty for the Fire. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And We will drive the criminals to Hell, thirsty and thirsty. They will be driven to it while they are thirsty and thirsty. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: I heard Sufyan say regarding His statement, And We will drive the criminals to Hell, thirsty. He said: Thirsty.
19:87: God Almighty says: These disbelievers in their Lord, O Muhammad, will not have the power to intercede on the Day when God will gather the righteous to Him as a delegation, when the people of faith will intercede for each other with God, and some of them will intercede for each other except for those among them who have taken a covenant with the Most Merciful in this world, with faith in Him, believing in His Messenger, acknowledging what he brought, and doing what he commanded. As Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Except for he who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, he said: The covenant is the testimony that there is no god but God, and he disavows before God any power and strength and hopes only in God. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement, They do not possess intercession except for one who has made a covenant with the Most Merciful, he said: The believers on that Day will be intercessors for one another, except for one who has made a covenant with the Most Merciful, he said: a righteous deed. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, They do not possess intercession except for one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful: meaning, by obeying Him. And he said in another verse, Intercession does not benefit except for one to whom the Most Merciful has given permission and whose word is acceptable (Ta-Ha 20:109) so that they may know that on the Day of Resurrection, God will intercede for some believers for others. “It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: ‘There is a man in my nation through whose intercession God will admit more people into Paradise than the Banu Tamim.’ And we used to tell stories about a martyr who would intercede for seventy of his family members. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu al-Malih, on the authority of Awf ibn Malik, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘My intercession is for whoever dies from my nation who does not associate anything with God.’” And min in his statement except for is in the accusative case as an exception, and it is not a genitive with the pronoun lam, but it may be in the accusative case in speech in a place other than this, and that is like the saying of the one who says: I wanted to pass by today except the enemy, for I will not pass by him, so he excludes the enemy from the meaning, and that is not the case in his statement: except for those who have taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, because the meaning of the statement is: These disbelievers do not have the power except for those who believe in God, so the believers are not from the number of disbelievers. And whoever puts it in the accusative case on the basis that its meaning is except for those who have taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, then his statement they do not have the power to intercede should be made for the righteous, so the meaning of the statement then is on the Day when We gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation, they do not have the power to intercede, except for those who have taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, so its meaning then is: except for those who have taken a covenant with the Most Merciful. The Most Gracious has made a covenant. But if he made they do not possess intercession a predicate for the criminals, then whoever would then be in the accusative case as a disjunctive exception, so the meaning of the statement would be: they do not possess intercession, but whoever takes a covenant with the Most Gracious has it.
19:88: God Almighty says: And these disbelievers in God said, The Most Gracious has taken a son. You have certainly done a terrible thing. God Almighty says to those who say that among His creation: You have certainly done, O people, a terrible thing in speech.
19:89: And similar to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying something great means: a great saying. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, You have certainly done something terrible, meaning: You have certainly done something terrible, which is the reprehensible speech. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, Ibn Abi Nujayh told us, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement something great he said: great. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, something great, he said: great. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, You have certainly done something terrible, he said: You have done something great in the matter, when they attributed a son to the Most Gracious. And there are three dialects for idd, it is said: Laqad ja’it shay’an iddan, with a kasra on the alif, and ada with a fatha on the alif, and ada with a fatha on the alif and a long vowel, on the example of mad fa’il. And the reciters of the regions read it, and we read it like that, and it was mentioned from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami that he read it with a fatha on the alif, but I do not see his reading it like that because it is different from the reading of the reciters of the regions. And the Arabs say for every great matter: id, “imr,” and nkar, and from it is the saying of the rajaz poet: The enemies have suffered from me a terrible, terrible and bitter punishment. And from it is the saying of another: In his panting and sluggishness if
19:90: And His saying, The heavens almost burst from it, the Almighty says: The heavens almost burst into pieces because of their saying, The Most Gracious has taken a son, and from this it is said: his fang burst: if it split. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, The heavens almost burst from it, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in devastation, because they attribute to the Most Merciful a son, he said: Indeed, polytheism terrified the heavens, the earth, the mountains, and all of creation except the two heavy ones, and they almost disappeared because of it due to the greatness of God. Just as the good deeds of the polytheist do not benefit with polytheism, so we hope that God will forgive the sins of the monotheists. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Teach your dead to bear witness that there is no god but God, and whoever says it at his death, Paradise is obligatory for him.” They said, O Messenger of God, but whoever says it when he is healthy? He said, That is more obligatory and more obligatory. Then he said, “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if the heavens and the earths and whatever is in them and what is between them and what is beneath them were brought and placed on one side of the scale, and the testimony that there is no god but God were placed on the other side, it would outweigh them.” Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, The heavens almost burst from it, the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in devastation. It was mentioned to us that Ka’b used to say: The angels became angry, and Hell was inflamed, when they said what they said. His saying, And the earth will split open, means: The earth will almost split open, and will crack from that. And the mountains will almost fall down in heap, means: The mountains will almost fall down on one another in a falling down. Falling down is the source of the verb threatened, so I will throw down a falling down. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And the mountains will collapse in ruins, meaning: demolition. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: And the mountains will collapse in devastation. He said: Devastation? The collapse. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And the mountains shall fall down in ruins, he said: In anger for God. He said: And those who made this for God, for whom the heavens, the earth, and the mountains were angry, called upon them to repent and said, They have certainly disbelieved who say, ‘God is the third of three.’ (al-Ma’idah 5:73) They said: He, his wife, and his son, they made them two gods. And there is no god except one God. (al-Ma’idah 5:73)... to His statement, And they seek His forgiveness, and God is Forgiving and Merciful. (al-Ma’idah 5:73)
19:91: God Almighty says: And the mountains almost fall down in a fit of turmoil, because they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. So, according to some Arab scholars, an is in the accusative case because of its connection to the verb, and according to others, it is in the genitive case with the prepositional pronoun - and we have explained the correct statement about that in more than one place in this book of ours - so that there is no need to repeat it in this place. He said, That they attribute to the Most Gracious a son, meaning by his saying, that they attribute: that they made a son for Him, as the poet said: Is there not a Lord whom you call to be sincere, and if you are absent you will find him absent and not sincere? Ibn Ahmar said: I love her with a sharp knife, and I make her shine, and I call her kohl-like dirt the monkey.
19:92: And his saying, And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son, means: And it is not befitting for God to take a son, because He is not like the creation who are overcome by desires, and are compelled by pleasures to have intercourse with females, and no child occurs except from a female, and God is exalted above being like His creation, and that is like the saying of Ibn Ahmar: In the head of a nobleman, a towering phoenix, beyond which there is no plain or mountain Meaning: It is not suitable and will not be.
19:93: There is none in the heavens and the earth but will come to the Most Merciful as a servant. He says: There is none in the heavens from the angels, and on the earth from the humans, mankind, and jinn but will come to the Most Merciful as a servant. He says: He will come to his Lord on the Day of Resurrection as a servant to Him, humbled and submissive, acknowledging servitude to Him, with no kinship between him and Him. And His saying I will come to the Most Merciful is only the subject of the verb I come to Him, so I will come to Him.
19:94: God Almighty says: The Most Gracious has counted all of His creation, and has counted them. Nothing is hidden from Him as to the number of all of them, and He knows their number, so not one of them is hidden from Him.
19:95: And all of them will come to Him alone on the Day of Resurrection. He says: And all of His creation will come to Him alone on the Day of Resurrection, with no helper from God, and no defender from Him. So God will decide concerning him what He will decide, and will do to him what He will do.
19:96: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who believed in God and His Messengers, and believed in what came to them from their Lord, and acted upon it, making lawful what He made lawful, and making unlawful what He made unlawful, the Most Merciful will appoint for them love in this world, in the hearts of His believing servants. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Yahya bin Talha told me: Sharik told us, on the authority of Muslim Al-Mala’i, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, The Most Gracious will bestow upon them love, he said: Love among people in this world. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, The Most Gracious will bestow upon them affection, he said: Love. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, The Most Gracious will bestow upon them love, he said: Love from the Muslims in this world, good provision, and a truthful tongue. Yahya bin Talha told me: Sharik told us, on the authority of Ubayd al-Maktab, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The Most Gracious will bestow upon them love, he said: Love among the Muslims in this world. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: The Most Gracious will grant them love, he said: He will love them and make them beloved to His creation. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, The Most Gracious will make for them love, he said: He will love them and make them beloved to the believers. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ali bin Hashim told us, on the authority of Abu Laila, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: He loves them and makes them beloved. Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us: Amr told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, The Most Gracious will bestow upon them love, he said: No servant turns to God except that God turns the hearts of the servants to him, and increases it from Him. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them love: Yes, by God, in the hearts of the people of faith. It was mentioned to us that Harim bin Hayyan used to say: No servant turns his heart to God, except that God turns the hearts of the believers to him, until He grants him their love and mercy. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, that Uthman bin Affan used to say: There is no servant among the people who does good or evil, except that God clothes him in the garment of his deeds. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, The Most Gracious will bestow upon them affection, he said: Love. And he mentioned that this verse was revealed about Abd al-Rahman bin Awf. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Saeed al-Wasiti told me: Yaqub ibn Muhammad told us: Abdul Aziz ibn Imran told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his mother Umm Ibrahim, daughter of Abi Ubaydah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, on the authority of her father, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, that when he migrated to Medina, he felt sorry for his companions in Mecca, including Shaiba ibn Rabi’ah, Utbah ibn Rabi’ah, and Ummatah ibn Khalaf. Then God Almighty revealed: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them love.
19:97: And His statement, We have only made it easy for you in your language that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous. God Almighty says: We have only made this Qur'an easy, O Muhammad, for you to recite, so that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous who fear God's punishment, by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience, of Paradise. And to warn with it a people who are obstinate. He says: And to warn with this Qur'an your people from Quraysh of God's punishment, for they are people of obstinacy and false argument, who do not accept the truth. And obstinacy means intense argument. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement Ladda he said: they do not stand upright. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And to warn with it a hostile people, meaning: to warn with it an unjust people. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And you warn with it a people who are argumentative with falsehood, meaning, who are stubborn and quarrelsome. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Muhammad bin Fadil told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And you warn thereby a hostile people, he said: wicked. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, a quarrelsome people, he said: arguing with falsehood. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And you warn thereby a hostile people, he said: The hostile is the unjust, and he recited the statement of God, And He is the most hostile of opponents (al-Baqarah 2:204). Abu Saleh Al-Darari told us: Al-Ala’ bin Abdul-Jabbar told us: Mahdi bin Maymun told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding the statement of God Almighty, And you warn thereby a people who are obstinate, he said: Deaf to the truth. Ibn Sinan told me: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the same. We have previously explained the meaning of al-ald with its evidence, so there is no need to repeat it here.
19:98: God the Almighty says: And many, O Muhammad, have We destroyed before your people from the polytheists of Quraysh. From a generation, meaning from a group of people, when they followed my opposition and committed the sins of their path. Do you sense any of them? He says: Do you sense any of them, O Muhammad, so that you see them and witness them or hear their sound meaning: Or hear their voice? Rather, they have perished and died, and their homes have become empty of them, and their dwellings have become desolate of them, and they have gone to a home in which nothing will benefit them except the good deeds they have done. So too are your people, they will end up in what those have ended up in, if they do not hasten to repent before destruction. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Or do you hear them making a sound? He said: A voice. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Do you perceive anyone from them or hear a sound from them? He said: Do you see an eye or hear a sound? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Do you sense anyone from them or hear a sound from them? He said: Do you hear a sound, or see an eye? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, in his statement, Or do you hear them making a sound? He meant: a voice. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The noise of the people is their voices. Abu Kuraib said: Sufyan said: Do you sense anyone from them or hear them making noise? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Do you sense anyone from them or hear a sound from them? He said: Or do you hear a sound from them. He said: And the sound is the sound. Abu Jaafar said: In Arabic speech, the word rakz means a low voice, as the poet said: So she was apprehensive about the mention of the companion, and it frightened her from behind her back, while the companion is her illness.
